headline: It's perfect for mature skin
comments: This is a wonderful foundation for mature skin because it is light adds a good bit of moisture to your skin. Most older women have drier skin and this is the answer! Looking at the reviews it seems like younger ladies are not happy with this product because they usually have oiler skin. I really love the coverage and it looks so sheer. I don't like covering it with a lot of powder.It is perfect by itself. If you have dry skin or are post menopausal this is your product! I also like the color selection. EstÃ©e Lauder is the only company that gets the colors right. If you have wrinkles like I do, apply and wait 5 minutes then wipe over(with your fingers) the lines on your face that the product has gathered in if any and then you are ready to go. I like to apply with my fingers. It seems to work best for me. I've tried so many foundations. This one is the best!

headline: GoodBYE Bare Minerals
comments: I've been using Bare Minerals foundation for over 25 years, started with the powder (the minerals activate when you swirl them with brush-remember that?) then to the liquid foundations. My usual BarePro in Fawn was nowhere to be bought so I read the mixed reviews (saw the brands moving away from makeup, no why?!) and took a chance on this. It comes out of pump thick, dries cakey like you bought some cheap drugstore brand and spackled it on your face. Bare Minerals is slacking on quality but keeping the prices up. Sadly I'll be breaking up with this brand and moving on.

headline: Good color
comments: The color was a perfect match but was a little too dry on my skin I need more of a moisturized product. I felt it looked pale in the sunlight and really dry looking although it is a matte cover.

headline: Bring back the old formula PLEASE
comments:
I used Bare Minerals for twenty years(using the liquids BarePro for at least 7). This new formula is terrible. I gave it the benefit of the doubt for two weeks. It ruined my skin. I have combination skin that leans on the dry side. This absolutely sucked any moisture out. I wish I could give it negative stars. 

I LOVE LOVE LOVE the old formula. BM, please bring it back!

headline: BRING BACK THE OLD FORMULA AND COLORS!
comments: This new formula is meh. Nothing really positive about it other than I found a color closest to me that actually looks natural to my skin but I miss the old formula only because I felt like it sits better on my face. It was better for my skin and this one dries and is flaky after putting on and after a while it doesn't look that great. I bought it to try it since the old formula went out, but I have now switched this foundation for a drugstore option which is a lot cheaper and the color I have for that is very close to the old shade I had with bareMinerals. So please bring back thd old formula.

headline: Drying and pore clogging
comments: My current foundation has been out of stock so I have been on the hunt for a new foundation. I thought I'd give this a try. On day three of using this foundation and my pores are so clogged. It's pretty drying too. I had high hopes as I thought bare minerals is not supposed to break your skin out. headline: Great for 40+ Skin
comments:
I am 40 with Roseccia on cheecks that tends to be dry, also have fine lines on forehead. 
I apply first my EL Serum then my Charlotte Tilbury Magic Cream and letvthat soaknin for 5-10 min. Then I applied 3 small pumps directly on checks and forehead and blended it out with a foundation brush, set with Laura Mercier loose powder as well the Irbam Decay Setting spray. Dabbed everything in once again with beauty blender! Like that I rceived a beautiful even complexion that lasted all day in the hot and humid weather of South Texas! 
It covered my mild roseccia well! If you have dark spots or more secerr redness you can combine this with concealer! 
I would highly recommend this to anyone that is looking for a light to medium buildable finish that diesnr settle in lines! Just make sure yiur skin is prepped first! EL never disappoints with their Foundations!

headline: Couldn't justify the price
comments:
This is a fine foundation. But I have way cheaper foundations that are just as good, if not better than this. I tested it for a month with different primers, sunscreens, powders, setting sprays, blush/bronzer/highlight etc, and rotated it with other foundations during the month. I took pictures and videos of my makeup every day (I know, obsessive lol) at different times of day so I could really analyze how good this product was on me vs my other foundations. I found that it was just fine, and I honestly couldn't differentiate it from my other foundations (which were all $14 and under). So I couldn't justify the price tag and returned it, which I've never done before. 
On the product itself - the consistency was a little thin and runny. I would call it more skin-like/satin than matte. Because of the thin consistency, it did settle into my fine lines. I have combo skin (oily tzone) and find that foundations tend to separate and wear off on my chin pretty quickly. This was no different. It didn't really separate throughout the day other than my tzone, again that's my experience with most of my foundations. I also found the shade to oxidize slightly/turn a little peachy on me - I'm fair and neutral/warm (typically foundations with slight yellow undertones work best on me) and got shade NC 13. 
Overall, I was really excited because this is only the second "expensive" foundation I've ever bought, and I've always heard great things about MAC. The first "expensive" foundation I bought was Lancome teint idole a couple years ago, and it was so beautiful and immediately felt and looked so special compared to my other foundations when I put it on. Even looking back at pictures, I could notice a difference when I had that on vs other foundations. I was hoping for a similar experience with this MAC foundation, and was really disappointed.

comments:
I have been using this foundation for at least 5 years and it was great - medium coverage and a shade that matches my face's neutral tones. Then, out of nowhere, L'Oreal redid the formulation from a 24HR to a 32HR bottle and continues to sell it under the same SKU. The shade and texture are completely different! I use 435 Rose Vanilla, and it's a nice neutral light-medium tone. The new 32HR has pink undertones and is at least 2 shades lighter than the original (closer to 410). The texture is also thicker and feels more like sunscreen. It doesn't settle and feels greasy after only an hour. 

I absolutely hate the new formulation! No one asked for Vitamin C in their foundation or to have 8 extra hours of coverage with a sunscreen texture. They should really be selling this under a new SKU, if they think there's a market for it, but I am very disappointed and annoyed that Ulta shipped me 4 bottles of the new one while still showing the old formulation's photos. Initially thinking it was just new packaging, I am now noticing there is a big difference in the quality when using it weeks later.

headline: Your Skin But Better
comments:
For reference, I'm in my 60's with normal skin, not oily, a teensy dry on my cheeks, forehead, and under my eyes, a few wrinkles, etc. In It Cosmetics I'm medium to medium tan. In the Clinique Beyond Perfecting I'm in CN52 and it is quite possibly the best match I've ever found in a cream / liquid foundation. 
B/c I love the ease, simplicity, and quickness of my powder foundations, I don't typically reach for a liquid or cream foundation - especially in the summer! But, I chose this as my "Diamond" reward â¦ and I am so pleasantly surprised!
I didn't care for the doe foot applicator at first â¦ however, it is NOT messy and I never have to get my fingers, or the back of my hand messy or goopy â¦ so I've decided it's a perfect idea! I dot it on, one area at a time, and use a brush for blending and application. It dries down very quickly, so I literally apply one area at a time. It's easy to build if needed. 
This truly could be the original "Your Skin But Better" look. I find it to be excellent coverage, blendable, and reliably and nicely long wearing â¦ even in our extraordinarily higher and more humid than normal, HOT, desert summer Vegas days. I dont find it to be cakey looking or settle into fine lines â¦ its just "Beyond Perfect" â¦ actually! 
I dont find this to be "dewy" looking but neither does it appear - or feel "drying." I dont have issues w/oily breakthru so I really can't speak to that. 
Lastly, if you're close to an Ulta, I would suggest trying it "in store" for your perfect shade. Just "picking" online, I got one too light the first time. And remember, Ulta has a flawless Satisfaction Guarantee so you cant lose giving it a try!

headline: Honestly didn't think I would like this
comments:
I have never really used powdered foundation until finding out about Natasha Denona's. As a fan of her eyeshadow, concealer, blush and eyeliners... I was amazed! 

It gives a nice natural coverage that is somewhat luminous. I will say, if you have enlarged pores or fine lines, you may have to find yourself reapplying to those areas. It did not accentuate your pores, but if you struggle with that area I would recommend a primer, as it didn't cover them up completely. It is great for covering redness, dullness and uneven skin tone! 

Personally after a 12 hour night shift of wearing this foundation, I would say it transferred minimally without a primer or setting powder. I used the elf power grip setting spray, and it helped seal the foundation better. 
It's super easy to blend contour, blush, bronzer and highlighter on top of this! 

I would give this a 94% satisfaction rate and recommend it to those with more normal, sensitive, combo or even oily skin types.

headline: Amazing
comments: I absolutely love this skin tint. I have normal, sensitive skin, but can be dry sometimes. I've never used foundation before, since my skin is extremely sensitive. headline: No Idea How This Product is so Highly Rated
comments: I have no idea how this product receives such rave reviews. It's a moisturizer, and provides zero coverage. It's not makeup. I visited an Ulta store, where I told them what my goals are (light-medium coverage, natural look, friendly to my aging millennial skin, buildable coverage when necessary, etc). Kudos to the associate - They did color match me exactly. However, after using this product myself at home, it literally does nothing. I even purchased the Hourglass setting powder to finish off the look, to no avail. And not only that! I used my usual makeup routine over top (eyelid primer, eyeshadow, eyeliner), and this Skin Tint is so "moisturizing" that even with my tried-and-true eyelid primer, my eyeshadow and eyeliner were all but gone by the end of the work day. I also had to use A LOT of this product to achieve even just the slightest bit of coverage. When I use my tried-and-true BB cream, I use mayyyybe a few little dabs to get the coverage I'm looking for. Needless to say, this will be going back to the store. No idea how this product made it through the testing phase and onto store shelves. It needs to be rebranded as a moisturizer, because it's definitely not makeup.

headline: This Pale Girl's Holy Grail!!
comments: I don't just throw the word holy grail around lightly!  This truly is THE BEST foundation I have ever tried and I've been searching for years.  If you are looking for a truly pale, neutral, full coverage formula with a natural finish and long wearing, this is the one!  I chose the very fair neutral shade.  At first swatch, I thought it was too light, but once it dries down it is the perfect neutral, buttermilk biscuit shade for this pale girl!  For reference, it is neutral but darker than Too Faced Snow and lighter than Swan.  In Nars, it is neutral and in between Siberia and Oslo.  Its closest match is L'oreal's 24 Hour Freshwear in shade 395 Rose Pearl, very, very close, but a much better more natural coverage.  I have mature, pale skin with pores on my nose, chin and cheeks that you can drive a truck through, but this covers them beautifully and blurs them out like magic.  I did prime my skin, ironically with NYX Liquid Putty Primer and even though this is a water based foundation, there was no separation or clashing.  With one pump worked into my foundation brush, it glided on and covered all my redness and sunspots, but looked like smooth skin and lasted all day.  I do powder with Dermablend loose setting powder and did touch up on my chin, nose and forehead with residual once during the day, but other than that, it remained perfect!  I am so impressed!!

headline: Foundation is amazing. Packaging sucks.

headline: Flawless & Feel Good Foundation
comments: Recently I went into Ulta to look for a new darker foundation for the summer. I was going to stick to what I had been using previously but saw the Polite Society Foundation on the display next to me. I'm obsessed with "good-for-you-skin-caring-foundations" and tried on a couple of shades in store. I finally settled on Light Neutral. For the past few days I've worn this foundation religiously! I only wear foundation occasionally because my skin usually gets irritated with everyday wear, but daily wear of this foundation has actually made my skin look better! I've changed nothing in my daily and nightly skincare routine that would aid in diminishing my acne, redness, and pores. It's led me to believe  that this foundation has actually been helping my skin! What makes it even better is it feels so lightweight going on, but provides so much coverage. I can't stand wearing foundations in the summer that feel heavy and greasy on the skin. I've worn this for 14+ hours and it still looks just as gorgeous as when I first applied it. I also did an ingredient search on all the individual ingredients to make sure the "clean" claims were true, and this foundation doesn't contain any overly irritating or dangerous/toxic ingredients like some other popular foundations. If you're looking for an all-around gorgeous, safe, and long lasting foundation, this is the one!

headline: It's good!
comments:
Coverage: It's not super full coverage, when I look for a face product I want something that can cover 5 o'clock shadow. This product on its own does not provide that for me and I still need to go in with concealer in those areas, but I know I'm asking for a lot when it comes to coverage. That being said it's still a step above medium coverage.

Wear: I have combo skin, this foundation doesn't make areas of my face feel like a grease trap at the end of the day and the claims of it being transfer proof for the most part hold up. Also haven't noticed any separation throughout the day when I get oily. You have to be pretty aggressive to notice traces of transfer. It's a water based foundation so used a water based primer with it.

Shade: I have issues finding shades that match my skin tone. I have a neutral-olive undertone but I am also pale. the Shade 006 was a shockingly great match for me, I'm satisfied with that.

Price: It's worth it in my opinion. Passes a lot of marks for me, would recommend this product and will be buying again.

headline: Five stars all the way!
comments:
I just tried the Chanel Les Beiges Water-Fresh Tint, and it's amazing! I usually don't wear makeup, but when I do, I keep it minimal with just blush and mascara. Every cosmetic product I've tried in the past felt heavy and uncomfortable. I've been searching for something light that enhances my skin without weighing it down, especially for special occasions and date nights. The Chanel Les Beiges Water-Fresh Tint is a game changer for me. The texture is incredibly light and refreshing, giving my skin a natural, dewy finish that feels like a second skin. The micro-droplet formula blends effortlessly and gives me a radiant, healthy glow without feeling heavy or cakey. It's perfect for achieving a no-makeup makeup look. I highly recommend this luxurious tint for anyone who wants to achieve a flawless, natural look. Five stars all the way!

I've uploaded a photo that I took about an hour after applying. I used no brushes or sponges when applying this. I blended the micro-droplets between my fingers and applied it like a moisturizer. I am honestly shocked at how incredible this product is. The fact that I put no effort into applying it, yet it somehow still turned out flawless, has blown my mind! I can't wait to see how incredible it looks and feels after prepping my skin and applying it with a brush and beauty blender.

headline: Worked Well on my Oily Skin

I prepped my clean face with the Fenty Pro Filt'R True Matte primer and then touched up some red areas of my face with the Pur 4-in-1 Redness Reducer Correcting Primer. After letting that dry, I went for it with a dry sponge. I chose color F10-C and it covered well, and not extremely thick. I powdered my face the new Glamlite Bake & Set Translucent powder. My face was matte with zero shininess coming though at all for the entire day! I live in south Texas where the humidity makes you sweat and "glisten" just sitting there! I did sweat, but there were zero streaks in my makeup! That's pretty much a first in my book! My skin didn't feel tight like it does when I put on all mattifying products. It felt good. Natural. I would recommend trying this foundation for any skin type. Just make sure you use a primer for your skin type.

headline: One of the Best
comments: I have not really loved a Chanel foundation since the original Vitalumiere which I loved. I have always struggled with shades in Chanel and they do tend to very greatly from one formula to another. I do not like matte foundation but I also don't prefer something that looks wet or greasy. This product is a great balance. It looks fresh with a lit from within glow. It is comfortable and also quite long wearing. The coverage is light but buildable which is my preference and I was able to get a pretty good shade match. It does have fragrance but it is not overwhelming. headline: On my Second Refill
comments:
I originally purchased the kit on the JE website, then came back to Ulta.com to get my refill. This is the only foundation I've ever actually used up!!! I have rosacea and wear glasses, so my tzone does get shiny and requires a small touchup at midday. Some tips:
-use a primer of some kind, either Jane's or another that you like.
-get a retractable travel brush (I use the one from Eco Tools) this is great for touchups and when I need more coverage, I twist the brush only halfway (making it denser) which gives more coverage for my cheeks because I have rosacea. If you need heavy coverage, you are going to want a dense brush to sort of pack it on in downward patting strokes. 
DO NOT swirl/buff...this is not the other mineral powder. different formulas work differently.

headline: Love this foundation!

I have very uneven skin, with broken blood vessels and acne scars that I used to spend far too much time trying to cover with concealer and/or heavy foundation. I've tried so many different brands and kinds of foundations, and they all look too heavy, unnatural and cakey. With this foundation, I only have to use a little bit to get the coverage I need, and it looks very light and natural. I also love how long lasting this foundation is, no matter what the weather, or how long my day is. As I've aged and have issues with texture and wrinkles, I've noticed this is the only foundation that doesn't settle into my wrinkles and fine lines. It smooths my pores, making me look airbrushed. Even though I sometimes stray to test trendy foundations with miracle claims, I always come back to Jane Iredale and the others end up in the trash. Can't get any better than this!

headline: Exactly what I was looking for!
comments:
The struggle with summer acne has been real, especially under a full face of foundation. After sweating on a hot day, I'm constantly battling clusters of little zits where the sweat gathers, specifically where my sunglasses sit on my cheeks. I started looking for a tinted moisturizer and every single one I came across had incredibly mixed reviews, but a large number complained of streaky application or little to no coverage. I finally stumbled across this one and the reviews were also mixed, a couple even saying it dried their skin out (weird for a moisturizer, right?). However, several reviews indicated that the coverage was actually pretty good, so I took the plunge. The shade match was pretty impressive considering there isn't many shades per skin tone. My first time using it, it went on so smooth, felt like I had nothing on, and gave a great medium coverage. 
I have dry skin, so the reviews claiming it dried them out had me concerned, but it did anything but. Maybe the people claiming that just didn't skin prep? Over the past few days, I've put it to work. I've gone out in the rain, I've worked up a sweat.. this stuff did not budge. I even braved a sweltering porta potty on a hot day (iykyk) and came out pouring sweat and it STILL looked good. Best part? No breakouts! How? Seriously how? This is now my holy grail for summer foundation. Obviously what works for me isn't always going to work for everyone, but my advice is definitely give this one a try if you're looking for a lightweight foundation that brings the coverage.

It can be built up for more coverage. It plays well with other products cream or dry or liquid. I enjoy using this foundation. It is also a perfect color match. I will repurchase and highly recommend trying it.

headline: PERFECT Summer Foundation
comments:
This is my one and only foundation for the summer season. It has the *wear* of the original Double Wear foundation, standing up to sweat and humidity like no other. If this foundation came out today I think it would probably be touted as a "skin tint" instead of a foundation. As the name suggest, the coverage is sheer. I like to use it as the first step in my makeup routine, working a light layer in really well before using a full-coverage concealer. Having this down as the base allows concealer and cream products to blend out flawlessly and lends its long wear and water resistance to formulas on top of it. I love how lightweight it is; I don't feel like I have makeup on at all and I can blend it down to my neck and chest easily. I also don't mind the extra spf! I also love that this sets to a natural finish that just looks like healthy skin.

I get the whole argument about light coverage formulas being more forgiving, but this line does not run light or dark enough - especially compared to the range of OG Double Wear. I can only wear this formula in the summer because it doesn't run light enough to match my Scottish-Welsh skin in the bleak mid-winter.

headline: PERFECT Summer Foundation
comments:
This is my one and only foundation for the summer season. It has the *wear* of the original Double Wear foundation, standing up to sweat and humidity like no other. If this foundation came out today I think it would probably be touted as a "skin tint" instead of a foundation. As the name suggest, the coverage is sheer. I like to use it as the first step in my makeup routine, working a light layer in really well before using a full-coverage concealer. Having this down as the base allows concealer and cream products to blend out flawlessly and lends its long wear and water resistance to formulas on top of it. I love how lightweight it is; I don't feel like I have makeup on at all and I can blend it down to my neck and chest easily. I also don't mind the extra spf! I also love that this sets to a natural finish that just looks like healthy skin.
My only complaint is the limited shade range. I get the whole argument about light coverage formulas being more forgiving, but this line does not run light or dark enough - especially compared to the range of OG Double Wear. I can only wear this formula in the summer because it doesn't run light enough to match my Scottish-Welsh skin in the bleak mid-winter.

headline: Reformulation is horrible
comments: I hated the thought of products reformulating because it usually is not for improvement. I used to get the 310 for winter & 312 for summer shades. Superstay was the drugtore Estee Lauder. this new formula in the 310 shade is a chalky, clay beige once it dries down. it is tricky to manipulate to peachy and golden undertones. one layer is chalky and dries quickly. two layers leans toward geisha with blemishes still visible. BTW, the first layer dries before you get to the second.  if you have to go to a third layer, almost mime. other products like concealer or liquid blush applied on top of the dried layers moisten the foundation and can put holes in it while trying to blend. other  products will blend in but it can be patchy. finishing up with a setting powder, and depending on its shade, gives the foundation a flat finish, without an undertone. It is not worth the struggle.

headline: For the price it's impressive
comments:
I've been a Bare Minerals Matte user for years, but the cost of a container has gone up to $40 and I found it necessary to retrench. I gave this makeup a shot. It's not as natural or smooth as Bare Minerals, and despite the greater options for color matching this Neutral tone 112 is much more bright yellow than my skin -- but it covers very well, I was quite impressed with that. It reminds me of a power foundation I bought circa 2001 from Hourglass (which cost $40 BACK THEN) so it's in the realm of the good quality stuff. It's just cakey, and it goes on unevenly with a tendency to clump up. I tried using the included applicator and it became all thick and gummed up before I finished applying a full face of makeup -- I use instead a dense, short-bristled brush for application, and tap it on, which gets better results over the pores. If you need to retouch a patch later on it's hopeless, you can't get the makeup even again (this is a common issue with powder foundation, even Bare Minerals.) 
All in all I'm unsure if I'd buy this again. It's less expensive than Bare Minerals but so are many things. If I get it again, I might try a Cool shade (even though I'm a Neutral) to see if it yields a closer hue, since the yellowish tone makes a  plain demarcation against my neck color (the cosmetic really needs more of a dull brown to balance it out.)

(Even the drugstore foundations I've tried perform better than this.)

I use a primer, setting powder, and setting spray. Here is my experience with this foundation:
-Within 2-3 hours it wears off no matter how I adjust my prep and finish 
-It immediately moves into my fine lines. Almost as if I put it only in them. It makes them look insanely worse. I will attach a picture if possible
-The makeup moves around my face the whole time I'm wearing it. After one smile I have ro wipe my laugh lines. Wearing less makeup hasn't helped. 
-No matter how I set it, it will come off with just one touch. On my husband's nose after a kiss, on my friend's cheek after a hug, on my daughter's finger when she "booped" my nose. 
-It is sticky the whole time I have it on no matter how I set it

The only good thing about this foundation is it initally blends really well. I don't mind spending money on makeup and use mostly all high-end items - but I wouldn't purchase this foundation even if it was $10. I fully believe the good reviews have been bought and the pictures have a filter on them. There's just no way someone likes this.

headline: Amazing foundation
comments:
I am truly blown away by this foundation! This is the first foundation in the past 5 years that I will continue using. For reference, i am 29 and have fair skin. 

I went in store and got shade matched and, for the first time, a foundation actually looks like my real skin. I have an elusive/inconsistent undertone, so it is typically very difficult to find any foundation that matches. 

The formula is exceptionally lightweight; it does not feel sticky or greasy. A thin layer provides a natural coverage and blurs imperfections and it can easily be layered for a natural buildable coverage without separating or settling into lines. 

It provides a light healthy glow but not extreme or something i would consider as "glowy," just a healthy natural-looking glow. I wore this foundation for the first time to the Nashville-Miami soccer game and it lasted 8-9 hours in the heat and humidity without any issues!!

Most importantly this foundation did not break me out. I have very sensitive skin and every foundation i have tried in the last 5 years caused a breakoutâ¦this did not!!!

The only "con" i would give this foundation is the high price, however that is to be expected with the brand; when i picked it in store, i did not know the price but i knew it would be in the $50+ because of the brand. I have been purchasing Chanel makeup since 2015 and am never disappointed. Also, i will note again that this foundation has good coverage so i am sure this bottle will last a long time. 

Finally, it does not seem to have a strong fragrance in my opinion. It does not have that classic Chanel makeup fragrance. There is a light/mild scent but one that is very faint and i feel dissapates after a minute on the skin. 

I HIGHLY recommend this foundation!!!!

headline: Beautiful
comments:
After countless high end and drugstore foundations, I have finally found the one. I have textured skin and most foundations look awful to begin with and then dont last on top of that. 
Camelia goes on smoothly- i used bare minerals pore minimizing primer underneath. Followed by IT concealer and the chanel cream bronzer.. guys i glowed in sc heat and it lasted for HOURS. buy this do not hesitate!!!!!!

headline: Very skin-like
comments: I've been wanting to try this for a while and finally pulled the trigger. It's very skin like. It does have a VERY luminous finish but not greasy or tacky. My skin is currently pretty dry, but I do have combination skin normally and think it would work for most skin types. Recommend getting shade matched in person if possible.

headline: Excellent foundation!
comments:
I love this foundation. It's light and feels nourishing. I was using a matte foundation (Chanel) for many years due to oily skin, but it started feeling kind of dry on my 60 y/o skin. My skin feels young again. And it glows. 
This one is a keeper!

headline: Magic in a Bottle
comments: Unlike any other foundation or concealer that I've tried.  Literally, this is magic.  Evens tone, covets flaws, smooths every textural flaw, diminishes pores, seems to moisturize any dry patches, and feels like I'm wearing no makeup.  It's absolute must-try for anyone over 50yo and doesn't love the typical look of foundation. Yes, I'm ordering a backup.

headline: Amazing
comments: I tried the Water Fresh Tint when it first came out and didn't like it at all. There was absolutely no coverage. This though, is what i was hoping for with the tint. The Complexion Touch is so good. It's beautiful on the skin and has a light to light medium coverage, and it feels like nothing on the skin. Don't use the brush that comes with it to apply because its way too small, however I've found that its a really good concealer brush. My only gripe with this foundation is that you go through it pretty fast. Im already halfway through my second bottle and this stuff is pricey. But it's totally worth it.

headline: Travel friendly

headline: Wow!
comments:
I purchased this online and did a swatch test on my chin - i couldn't even tell where i swatched when i looked in the mirror because it blended so well. The color match was spot-on! I used the Ulta shade finder and landed on BD91 - I currently wear Too Faced in Maple or MAC NC47. The product goes on smooth and is lightweight, and it comes with a small dome brush that i didn't care for. My fingers and a blending sponge worked fine. 

Cons: I noticed some oxidation which made my face a little orange. I used a primer with sunscreen, which made it worse, but even without there still was a slight orange i noticed after having it on a few hours. The bottle is small - 20ml for the price. Most brands offer 30ml sizes.

headline: This the One
comments: I have dry, sensitive skin and have been on an endless search for a foundation that provides coverage, does not look caked on, lasts throughout the day, and most importantly, does not break me out. I was starting to believe my wish list was too long, but this one delivers on all. It does take some getting used to with application. I find I like it best when I smear 2-3 pumps on the top of my hand and blend, then use a dense brush for application. It wont look like heavy coverage at first, but give it a minute to settle into your skin. After adding powder, its a flawless finish. (Shades are not exact matches for me, so I blend 2. I have warm/yellow undertones and find that shade 20 + 60 is a beautiful mix. Another option is to just use the lighter shade and apply a slightly darker powder). I use the water blush in Warm Pink and my face looks hydrated, beautiful, and blemish-free all day long. Love it! I have found the One!

headline: LITERALLY THE BEST
comments:
I'm gonna give some main points and then elaborate because I have so much to say about this foundation.

1- it is a buttery smooth application
2- it gives the prettiest subtle glow, but it's somehow still soft matte
3- it IS transfer-proof if you set it with powder and/or setting spray

As far as the shade range- I always have to mix my foundations anyway so it doesn't really bother me. In response to it transferring- most non-ultra-matte foundations do. So like with every other, if you use powder or a good setting spray (or both) then you're good to go. 

I have oily-combination and sensitive skin, and this is my favorite foundation out of everything I've ever tried. I honestly didn't want to love it so much because it's much more expensive than I'd like, but I've tried to replace it and nothing works or looks as well. I have a lot of acne scarring, but people always say my skin looks so smooth and clear with this on. I love using it with the mineral veil primer and together they are just 🤌🤌 I highly highly recommend.

headline: replaced my HG Backstage foundation
comments: Just when I thought I would wear Dior Backstage forever, I found this beauty... and it's my perfect foundation! I was really nervous purchasing this one (and not just for the price, although it's not inexpensive) because 1, there wasn't a single YouTube review about it (even from my favorite Dior-loving, Ulta -loving ones) and 2, I was matched with a very different shade than in my Backstage color (0.5 in Backstage, I was recommended 1.5 in this formula). Without any photos of anyone who looked much like me, I put my trust in the "shade finder" guide and bought it with some of my Ulta rewards points.  Now I'm going to have to cough up the $$$ when I need to replace it because it's my favorite foundation ever! It's got light-to-medium coverage that I want, it blurs my texture (fine lines, pores and wrinkles) while it moisturizes just enough and leaves a pretty, natural glow to my skin (not shimmer, certainly not glitter... just the glow of youth and vitality that tends to dim a bit with age). And one to one and a half pumps does my whole face (I don't have a petite face either lol) which makes me confident a bottle will last awhile. This foundation makes me feel good about how my 50+ skin looks and the shade match is chef's kiss perfection. I've stopped looking at any other foundation... this one is my new Holy Grail!

headline: Perfect Glowy Skin Tint for the Summer
comments: This skin tint is perfect for my dry skin! With summer coming, I walked into Ulta wanting something that wasn't super full coverage and would give me a nice glowy look for the summer. I tested this out in the store and loved the glow it gave me! It feels super hydrating on the skin, like if you were to put a moisturizer on it. If you have oily or combo skin, this tint may be a but much for you and make your skin seem too dewy, but you can play it down with a good setting powder where you get oily. I know some of the other reviews have overwhelmingly had issues with the cap breaking off, I have not yet experienced this. Also, If you are looking for this to cover every blemish and spot on your face, I would not recommend this product for you, as it's meant to act as a natural, radiant glow boosting serum for the skin with just a hint of tint. If you're a chronic dry-skin girly, I think you'll be pleasantly surprised by how nice this makes the skin look. It's worth a try!

headline: A little goes a long way!
comments:
I'm a medium cool neutral skin tone with oily combination skin - 540 Giza.
I layer usually with additional contouring darker shades to warm up my skin tone and add more dimension, but it's very light, minimual layering, as I do not like to wear anything heavy.

This foundation is awesome! I L O V E it because of how much a little goes a long way. I tend to prep my skin with moisturizer and primer for smoother application. I tend to apply light layers, which may be way this product has lasted so long for me - I do not like thick layers, nor do I feel that I need to layer so much of the product to get decent coverage. It has a nice mattifying effect, but does not accentuate lines or cause any unflattering crepe-y undereye area. If you're looking for something "glowy" or something of a pearlescent finish like a CC cream or tinted moisturizer, this may not be for you - it is quite mattifying, and despite my light handed application (like I mentioned earlier, a little goes a long time), it does offer good coverage without the cake-on effect. 

In pictures, it helps my face look more even and helps with my shiny t-zone area. 

I got these when they were 50% off, and had purchased 2. I know my first tube I'm currently on is nowhere close to being out, but I do wear foundation only on special occasions. 

I live in hot humid Texas, and have yet to experience any breakout with this product.

headline: hated it in 2021; now a fan in 2024!
comments: I purchased the Dermablend Flawless Creator Liquid Foundation Drops in 2021 and HATED it with a passion. It was cakey, flakey, and emphasized all my lines and creases. It was just a complete mess. I typically use mineral foundation but I've been wanting to try liquid foundation so I decided to give these Foundation Drops another try because they are one of the few liquid foundations that is 100% cleared for acne-prone skin. (I have sensitive skin, hyperpigmentation, and acne so I am overly cautious and extremely vigilant about ingredients listed in foundations, particularly liquid foundations. I always check the ingredients list against verified online acne-safe ingredient/product check tools.) I dunno what the heck happened, but I am now a FAN of these Foundation Drops. For some bizarre reason, it is NO LONGER cakey or flakey and it NO LONGER emphasizes any fine lines or wrinkles. How?! It's so freakin' easy to apply and a little goes a LONG way. I just use 1-2 drops (no joke) and I blend with my fingertips. Those 1-2 drops covers my entire face as if it's full-coverage foundation. It actually DE-emphasizes any fine lines and wrinkles and it covers all my hyperpigmentation and scarring. How?! I'm a light-medium neutral skin tone so I purchased 37N, 40N, and 43N. I'm either a true 40N or a blend of 37N and 43N (probably 43N in the summertime). That said, I haven't tested whether this is sweat-proof and I haven't worn this all-day yet - so not sure how it holds up in terms of wear and waer. But, for events and occasions, this might be my new fave foundation. If you're on the fence about trying this out, I'd say, give it a go. I'm still in shock that I am no longer hating on these Foundation Drops. Here's to successful second chances!

headline: Not Worth The Money
comments: I normally love Pat McGrath makeup, and find it to be worth the price. However, I can't say the same for the foundation. I've tried applying it with different brushes/sponges, with/without primers, and/or setting sprays. No matter what I do, it doesn't wear well on my skin. First off, it's quite runny. It applies patchy/streaky, so I feel like I realy have to work with it. Then, within a short amount of time it begins to settle into any lines and separate, especially around my nose. I definitely won't be purchasing this again.

headline: Perfect for Mature Skin
comments: I went through bottles of other foundations, high end and drugstore before I came across this one. I got it as a sample first. I thought just try it out, see how it goes and fell in love with it. It glided perfectly onto my skin, so lightweight and blended naturally. It doesn't settle into my fine lines or wrinkles and feels like I am wearing nothing on my skin. I don't like heavy foundations or makeup on my skin, so this was perfect. I get so many compliments now on how great my makeup looks, all thanks to this foundation! Love it!

headline: A great foundation for natural look
comments: This foundation is good for those that want a natural look with a hint of radiance. Full coverage users stay away. I use 1-1/2 pumps (yes a half) and it is the perfect amount . The foundation is pretty runny but is surprisingly pigmented for a light to medium coverage. It appears to have a self setting effect too. Those who have dry skin just make sure that you moisturize well and you are good. This doesn't oxidize at all. I have the shades 23 and 26 both are for (golden) olive tones. Perfect undertones for me. Foundation works well with non PML makeup/skincare products. Now yes this is a pricey one. I'm a picky foundation wearer because of foundation coverage/thickness preferences , my undertone and dry skin. I dont want to buy multiple products to make a foundation work. I'll pay a little more for a product to have everything I want in one bottle and this does it for me. Will definitely purchase again.

headline: Light Medium 14 for Olive Undertone
comments:
I am so glad PM Labs is now being sold in Ulta. This foundation has become a favorite.

My shade is Light Medium 14 - on the website it is described as Light Medium with Neutral Olive Undertones.
Skintype: Oily, Very Sensitive

I find the undertone to not be the best for someone with an olive undertone, I swatched many shades and in-person and they were all a bit too yellow. But if you mix a little blue color corrector, you may be able to get a closer match.

The consistency and feel of this foundation on the skin, is nothing like I have experienced before. The formula is extremely thin, but can be layered multiple times to build coverage or just refresh your base. I love building the coverage, and I am AMAZED at how the foundation is able to look like skin! Usually foundations with a similar consistency are very light coverage and if buildable, layering would look heavy on the skin.

Pat only uses her brand and this foundation, specifically, on the set of Bridgerton - and every actor's base is always flawless so I wanted to try it. If you can find your perfect match/shade, you will lovee this.

headline: Very Skin-like and Luxurious
comments:
I've received a lot of compliments on my skin when wearing this foundation and been told my skin looks glowy. This foundation does a great job at leaving a "lit from within glow" and does not look greasy at any point during the day. It leaves more of a satin finish and does not completely matte down. 

This foundation has a runnier consistency than a skin tint. That being said, it does make it easier to blend out. For being a thin formula, it's actually pretty pigmented. I need about 1-2 pumps of product for my entire face and it blends beautifully with a stippling brush. I've also been able to blend this with just my fingers or a sponge as well. I have not tried the primer that goes with it but I typically use the Bobbi Brown Vitamin Enriched Face Base with the PMG foundation and found they work well together. 

The bottle looks and feels very luxurious. I have noticed however that I've been running out of product a little but faster compared to other liquid foundations I've used. For the price point, this foundation needs to apply itself and pump my gas for me. This is a good foundation if you have a coupon that applies to prestige and you want to treat yourself to something more high-end but I wouldn't pay full price for this foundation.

headline: New Summer Staple
comments:
I have been on the hunt for an affordable tinted SPF of sorts for the wicked summer heat and decided to give this one a try. When I first tried it, it had a bit of a strange chemical-like smell which I attributed to the SPF actives; it doesn't smell sunscreen-like or bad necessarily, just a bit odd (I do tend to use mineral SPF though, so it could very well be normal!). I tried this on a 100 degree day of work and an evening out, and it held up really well with no caking and minimal shine (I only touched up with powder once!). It is truly lightweight and looks skinlike with a healthy radianceânot overly dewy or glowy; perfect for a natural everyday, summery look. I had no issues with oxidiation like many others have shared, however, I did not spend much time in the direct sunlight. Besides the odd smell, the only other word of caution I would provide is that it pills badly depending on how you apply it: I don't recommend applying directly to the skin; instead, I sprayed a brush with setting spray, both applying and blending with the brush. When I did it this way, my base was beautiful!! 

Overall, I can excuse the smell for what good quality it is, and as long as you apply it correctly, it is definitely a great buyâespecially compared to other SPF skin tints on the market!!

*Applies well with brushes or sponges, but better with your fingers.

headline: great!
comments:
I recently tried the Makeup Revolution IRL Filter Longwear Foundation and while it has some great features, it didn't quite meet my expectations. On the positive side, the foundation has a soft focus breathable matte formula that allows you to achieve a flawless finish at the level of coverage you desire. The formula is also oil-free, shine-free, crease-proof, lifeproof, and smudgeproof, so it's perfect for those who need a long-lasting foundation. The super coverage with 20% more pigment makes it easy to build and blend the foundation for the coverage you desire. The foundation is housed in a luxe glass bottle with a built-in pump, making it easy to apply. I also appreciate that it's cruelty-free and vegan, with key ingredients like niacinamide, which is great for your skin.

However, I did find some drawbacks to the foundation. While it claims to provide a "filter in a bottle" look, I didn't find that it lived up to this promise. Additionally, I found that the foundation didn't blend as easily as I would have liked, and it tended to settle into my fine lines and wrinkles, making them more noticeable. Overall, I would give this foundation 3 stars - it has some great features, but it didn't quite meet my expectations in terms of achieving a flawless, filter-like finish

headline: Easy everyday product
comments: I ordered this online because my local store rarely carries products for my extremely fair skin. Not gonna lie - the product looked way too dark and peachy for my pale cool complexion. But I tried it and I'm so glad I did! I'm sure if I had seen this in-store I would have passed it up. I started with my serum and skin cream and after that set for a couple minutes I applied this balm with a small hybrid foundation brush. The product is really easy to work with. It's kind of a one and done product. The coverage is light so I had to go back with the concealer crayon to cover up some hyperpigmentation - but I have to do that with medium buildable coverage products too. I didn't set it with powder afterward, but I did apply a bit of blush, a little bronzer and highlighter - all powder products. I did this very lightly so that I didn't disrupt the balm underneath. I misted with setting spray and got on with my day. This lasted a good 10 hours and then it started to break down and fade, but it didn't settle in my pores or fine lines. My only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is the packaging. It makes sense for a balm to be in a jar, but I had to keep putting my foundation brush back into it and I worry that the product might get contaminated. I don't know if there's a way to put it in a squeeze tube, but that would be ideal for me.

headline: I found my dream foundation!
comments:
I have been on a journey to find the perfect foundation for my oily, early 30s, very pale skin. 
Something light coverage, that just evens out my skintone and dulls the redness. A light layer that easily applies over sunscreen, that will last all day. I'm so happy I finally found this product! 
It checks all of my boxes and then some!
Very natural looking finish, goes on easily, and I don't have to spend an eternity blending. I was able to achieve a great look with just my fingers.
They nailed the tone for us pale folks too, no orange at all!
Be aware this has VERY light coverage, I can actually still see my freckles through it. I absolutely love that, but if you are looking to hide anything, this probably won't do it for you. 
It has an accurate name because it comes out of the bottle just like milk. I actually made a mess on my counter applying it the first time because I wasn't expecting such a watery consistency, you've been warned!
It feels very nourishing and weightless, almost like moisturizer. The only con I can think of is I wish the bottle was bigger.

Overall an affordable, light coverage foundation that feels like you aren't even wearing it.

headline: Love the product but NOT vegan
comments:

But I'm SO disappointed that it is not a vegan product and getting frustrated that ULTA continues to tag products as vegan when they clearly contain animal by-products. Cruelty free is awesome, but it simply means that the products and ingredients aren't tested on animals. It does NOT mean that the product is free of animal-derived ingredients. If you care about animal welfare (and don't want to waste your dollars) check the product manufacturer site or a reputable vegan source. 

ULTA, please correct all of your vegan categorization errors. Will not be ordering from your site again.

The color match is great, no quarrels there. It is also a great base for makeup and blends very smoothly with a beauty blender. I am, however, disappointed in the coverage. It is a very sheer foundation - it mostly just does color correction and levels out skin color. It does not do much for acne scars or dark circles. Also make sure to exfoliate and moisturize, as this will cling to dry patches. It also seems to fade a bit throughout the day.

Overall, it's a decent tinted moisturizer. Look elsewhere for lightweight with coverage.

I have both very oily and very dry skin and zero skin care routine so a lot of that is likely due to me being a bit terrible. But I was randomly recommended this over a year ago by a guy at the mall of America morphe store and it genuinely felt like second skin. He paired it with morphe primer and it's the best my skin ever has or will look. It looks so natural and yet makes my skin look amazing. You can't even tell I'm wearing foundation. 

I sadly ran out and tossed the bottle before ordering more like an idiot and I've spent the last 5 months trying to track this foundation down. I just ordered more so unless the formula has changed drastically I'll add pictures once I have it. But I was genuinely mourning the loss of this foundation and thought I was doomed to have cakey looking skin again forever. 

If you can't find a foundation no matter how many you try I highly highly recommend this one. Maybe my skin is just weird so it might not work for you but I will never ever allow myself to run out of this foundation again. It's been a terrible few months for my makeup without it.

headline: a major miss
comments:
I was so excited to try this product, as stick foundations are really convenient and that's a huge plus for me.  I deal with both hormonal and anxiety issues, both of which cause me to occasionally sweat excessively, specifically my face.  The name of this, "active" foundation, plus its claims to be sweat proof, gave me high hopes.
Unfortunately, this foundation misses so many marks.  First of all, the shade range is embarrassing.  There is no excuse for brands to exclude women of color in their products.  Aside from that, this product does not sit nicely on the skin.  It clings to dry patches, settles in pores, and emphasizes texture and peach fuzz.  I gave it many chances, making sure to properly exfoliate and moisturize beforehand.  No matter what I did, it looked terrible.  Also, I would not say it is sweat proof, in the fact that this product easily transfers off, and if you're sweating, you're most likely going to either blot or wipe the sweat away.  Upon doing so, this product completely wipes away very easily.
Finally, I think they missed the mark by not including at least a bit of SPF protection in this, being it's called their "Active" foundation, and that sort of implies it can/should be worn during a multitude of outdoor activities.
I left two stars as opposed to one for the convenience of the application in a stick.

headline: Love this foundation!
comments:
I have very fair and pink skin and have always had trouble finding foundations that match my tone, never mind work well on my oily/combination skin, but I will say that this one does a good job! I was nervous buying online without match testing, but I got the 1C and would say its a pretty good match for my skin tone. 

My pros for this are definitely: generaly matches my skin, works well with my oily/combination skin, it coming in a stick format is very convenient and mess free, stays on very well, looks natural, and doesnt make my skin feel gross

My cons would be: not the perfect match (wish the undertones were more p and that the shade was slightly lighter), can get a little cakey if i put too much on, and a little hard to blend. 

For context I've been wearing Too Faced Born this way foundation in the shade Snow for years now because it's the only foundation I've found that comes close to matching my skin, but I've always run into the same problem of not being able to apply the foundation too thick because then you can tell it's not a true match. Anyway, I would say overall thi one does a better job, has better ingredients, feels better on my skin, and is a good price point.

My last points would be dont let the 1 star reviews scare you, this foundation is very nice and as long as you use a wet sponge to apply and don't mind the mild scent of castor oil that fades in about 30 minutes :)

It dries down slightly and feels like a moisturizer. I didn't set it since it dries down to a semi-matte finish, but you may need to if you want it to last longer. I still moisturized and used sunscreen underneath and it wore very nicely. It's very lightweight and doesn't look cakey, just an evened out skintone. I really like this! Will probably lighten if I use a lighter setting powder.

headline: My all Time Favorite
comments:
I used to never finish a bottle of foundation because I would hust keep getting new ones to try, I usually had atleast 6 at a time. However, I dont overconsume like I used to thankfully, especially when it comes to makeup. 
That was 3 years ago before I tried this one and its been 2 years now that I have only used and bought this foundation. 

Its my favorite foundation that ive ever used! Everything about it works so well with my skin. I got compliments all the time about how good my skin looked and I was always wearing this. 

Its super creamy and easy to nove around and blend on the skin. It doesnt cling to my numerous dry patches, its luminous without being oily. Its the PERFECT amount of coverage. I hate full coverage foundations but I need more coverage than just a skin tint. Its right between a light and medium coverage I'd say. Although it is buildable, I rarely applied more than one layer. 

The stick format streamlined my makeup routine SO well. Yes I wish there was more product in it, but that is my ONLY complaint.

Im gutted this is being discontinued, but I kind of saw this coming. Every time it would go on sale I'd worry, and now its for real being discontinued which is sooooo sad. 

There is like NO other stick foundations out there like this one, and ones that are actually comparable are of course high end. Like the Hourglass one which is so expensive, especially when considering how often you have to repurchase these kinds of foundations. Ya that is not happening, in this economy? Bffr

headline: New Formula Ruined my Favorite Powder Foundation
comments:
Wow. I've been using makeup for 25 years and seen a lot of industry hits and misses, but never have I seen a great product RUINED by a new formulation like this baked foundation. 

WHY would anyone think it was a good idea to add bits of sparkly mica to a previously matte foundation product? Who do you think is buying this? Not all your clientele is under 30, or even 40. Sparkly foundation highlights skin imperfections. 

This should have been offered as a different product since it is clearly for an entirely different audience and set of skin concerns- ones that are clearly at odds with the needs of your established, previously happy customers. Very disappointing.

It evens out my skin way more than I expected, super pleased with the natural looking coverage as I get cakey easily. I've also noticed the transfer is minimal unless rubbed, so it's pretty sunglasses and glasses friendly! Love it!

headline: HIDDEN GEM !!!
comments: Hidden Gem hands down. I have been looking for a good foundation in general for a few years now, I went high end low end drugstore I went tinted moisturizer to full coverage and non did what I actually wanted. I love make up but finding a good foundation for my oily skin that wont force me to re touch (which I'm horrible at by the way, always makes it worse) was close to impossible without making me feel like I have pounds of make up on especially for work. I had tried the Hourglass foundation stick which was highly rated and felt very chalky on my skin. I did a search of stick foundations and came across this one. I am the lightest shade in this line and am on my way to re up for a 3rd time! I have never purchased 1 item more than once since they end up not working out for a while. The coverage is amazing from one layer to a 2 layers if I want a fuller look. It glides on like butter on my skin  and gives me a glow without an oily look if that makes sense. I rarely have to completely set my face because it sets so nice on its own and will literally last me over 9 hours without any cracks or separation and looks like I just applied it minutes ago. It makes my face feel hydrated and not like I'm wearing loads of make up. This is a long review and I never leave a review but I am truly in love with this foundation! I am so thankful for this brand because I am the in between when it comes to make up, I'm a semy fare complexion with neutral undertones. Many lines have a Yellow undertone or an olive undertone which makes me look washed out. This is truly a bang for your buck and will leave your make up looking flawless.

headline: Nice, but...there are application & color issues.
comments: This is a nice powder (shade: Ivory), but I found the application to be cakey & unnatural-looking when applied with the sponge. I actually almost returned it because of this, but then I decided to apply it with a brush instead, and it was much better, so I kept it. However, this probably will not be a repeat-buy for me because I found the lightest shade (Ivory) to be a bit too golden/yellow for my skin (and my skin has yellow undertones!) The color mismatch was more obvious when using the sponge, but is workable with the brush, being that brush application makes the powder more sheer. I wish they had a fuller range of fair/light shades like the Infallible powder, which offers Pearl and Porcelain as lighter options. If this powder was offered in Porcelain, I would have chosen that one instead. I like that this power is fragrance-free (the Infallible isn't, for some reason), and does have a nice satin finish on the skin. The brush works for me because I don't need a lot of coverage, but if you need fuller coverage you MAY find that a thicker application (for example, with a sponge) will result in a less-than-natural looking result.

headline: A foundation that actually matches me!!!
comments: I bought this foundation in the color A06. I tend to have a hard time finding foundations because I am in the weird shade range where I'm typically between medium/tan and dark/deep in various brands. I have Neutral slightly golden/olive undertones and find that many brands get close but not perfectly my shade. Most times foundations are too golden (almost orange looking), too cool, exactly neutral when I need just a touch of yellow in the foundation, or they just skip my shade altogether. I was pleasantly surprised when this foundation was an exact match. I love the natural finish to this foundation. I have dehydrated combo skin that if not properly hydrated will get oily in the t-zone (mostly nose area) and will remain normal or slightly dry everywhere else. When I wear this for several hours my foundation goes from very natural to radiant but not oily as my t-zone starts to break into a bit of a shine. I really don't have anything bad to say about this foundation except because of the limited shade range there's a chance you may not find a good match depending on your skin tone and undertone. Hopefully Ulta continues to keep this foundation available.

I have dry/combo skin but mostly dry and just very sweaty ALL THE TIME because I have hyperhydrosis. I wore this from 7am to 9pm and it was BEAUTIFUL. Minor wear on my problem area on chin around mouth but I just bring a tiny concealer brush to push back into place. I even wore through an intense workout and lasted amazing. I am shade V02 & I would say it leans a little peach on my fair olive skin but I mix in color to make it match me (NC12/NC13) I just wish it didnt have spf because I already wear spf under my makeup but I havent tried a flash test yet. Will report back.

headline: DEFINITELY GET IT!

I also tried mixing V05 & V04 to get my shade if anyone is wondering. I hope this helps.  :)

headline: Fantastic for the right user
comments: "CC cream" is a misnomer, as that is not what this product is. It doesn't have enough coverage for that. That said, it's a phenomenal product for the right skin type and for those who like a 'barely there' make up look. It's very thick and a bit oily, so ladies with dry or mature skin, or folks who live in the desert or places with harsh dry winters, will appreciate this. It provides minimal coverage, but just enough to give the skin a hydrated sheen and tone down any redness. I think of it as a low-coverage skin tint for dry or dehydrated skin. The physical sunscreen is effective but, as others have said, you'd have to use a lot of the product to get full protection and it's too heavy for that so I wouldn't rely on it for SPF. It has a strong botanical scent, I happen to love it, and it does not irritate my sensitive skin. The shade range is decent, again because the coverage is minimal. You can't really go wrong with a color match, just focus on the undertone and the rest will sort itself out. I gravitate toward this product on winter days when I don't want to wear make up but want my skin to look refreshed and hydrated. It's comparable to the Jones Road WTF foundation but with less coverage, to give you a sense of texture and richness. And I like that it comes in a tube, not a pot, for hygienic reasons. The head of the tube can break if you're not careful with how hard you squeeze the product, just one of those things you get used to over time. It fills in my fine lines really well and plumps up my skin, doesn't settle or separate. It stays a bit tacky for 20-30 minutes, depending on how much you use, then absorbs. I've bought several tubes over the years and will always have one around for days when it's just what my skin craves. Folks with oily skin, folks in humid, climates, folks who don't like scented products, folks who want significant coverage should avoid this product.

headline: I love it but see why others might not
comments:
First, I personally really like this product but it does have its flawsâ¦ some of the reasons I love it might be reason why someone else might not like it at all. 

1) It is scented like all Juice Beauty products, that funky citrus scent that lingers. I use several products by this brand and they all smell the same.  It doesn't bother me, but if you're sensitive to fragrance, try a sample first. 

2) The texture is creamy but thick, making it harder to blend into the skin. In my opinion, its worth the effort and looks very natural once blended in, but if you dont like blending with fingers, it could be frustrating. I blend/apply with fingers then finish by pressing into my skin with beauty blender. A thick application can leave a sticky, tacky finish, so I prefer a light layer, then build up another layer in same way if needed. 

3) The finish is quite shiny. I have dry skin, so it ends up looking like healthy hydrated skin for me. But heavier applications or too thick layers can look odd, and can emphasize texture and fine lines. But light layers worked into your skin well, you can achieve a very natutal, beautifully healthy appearance to your skin. 

4) The coverage on this is light. Buildable only slightly before the thick texture gets unflattering. So if you need more coverage, this isnt worth your funds or time. I prefer a light coverage product for day to day wear, so this works well for me. 

5) As creamy, thick, and shiny as this is, its not super hydrating. I have dry skin snd still need a separate moisturizer under this or my skin can get flaky after wearing this a few days in a row. 

6) This has spf but I'm not using this as my only sunscreen, because to get the correct amount on your skin for the full spf benefits, its way too much of this product. See above for how it looks when applied too thickly. 

So overall, its a finicky product that happens to work well for me but I hesitate to recommend because the potential for failure is definitely there.

headline: Looks good at first, but turns blotchy very quickly.
comments:
Over 50 - Oily/Combo Skin with some large pores: I had high hopes for this product when I bought it, and even went into it understanding that color matching would be a challenge. I actually bought two colors, fair and medium, and custom blended them for a better match. I applied it first with my fingers, but turned to first a foundation brush for more even application, and then a damp makeup sponge to further even it out. At first I absolutely loved the look, which was light, natural and looked like healthy skin. The product felt weightless and offered enough coverage to tone down some of my imperfections while still allowing the natural pink flush of my cheeks to come through. But the fresh skin look didn't last. Within an hour my skin started to look greasy, orangey and cakey in my pores and fine lines. I blotted and dusted the T-zone with a finishing powder, but the airbrushed effect only lasted about 30 minutes before the shine returned and my pores and wrinkles were again obvious.

My second application I decided to apply a pore minimizing, matifying primer to my skin first. I still had to use makeup tools to get the best application, and the fresh skin look definitely lasted longer, but the product still broke down after just a couple hours. (I skipped using powder this time.)

I have also tried using setting spray to prolong the initial clean-skin look, but to no avail. My conclusion is, if you have younger, non-oily skin, I think this product would be a real winner. If you have lines, wrinkles, enlarged pores and oily skin, I doubt you'll be happy with the results on your face. It does, however, make a nice tinted moisturizer for you neck and decollete to help match your face after applying foundation. And a little setting spray on top keeps the BB Cream from transferring to your clothing.

headline: Exactly what I was looking for!
comments:
The struggle with summer acne has been real, especially under a full face of foundation. After sweating on a hot day, I'm constantly battling clusters of little zits where the sweat gathers, specifically where my sunglasses sit on my cheeks. I started looking for a tinted moisturizer and every single one I came across had incredibly mixed reviews, but a large number complained of streaky application or little to no coverage. I finally stumbled across this one and the reviews were also mixed, a couple even saying it dried their skin out (weird for a moisturizer, right?). However, several reviews indicated that the coverage was actually pretty good, so I took the plunge. The shade match was pretty impressive considering there isn't many shades per skin tone. My first time using it, it went on so smooth, felt like I had nothing on, and gave a great medium coverage. 
I have dry skin, so the reviews claiming it dried them out had me concerned, but it did anything but. Maybe the people claiming that just didn't skin prep? Over the past few days, I've put it to work. I've gone out in the rain, I've worked up a sweat.. this stuff did not budge. I even braved a sweltering porta potty on a hot day (iykyk) and came out pouring sweat and it STILL looked good. Best part? No breakouts! How? Seriously how? This is now my holy grail for summer foundation. Obviously what works for me isn't always going to work for everyone, but my advice is definitely give this one a try if you're looking for a lightweight foundation that brings the coverage.

headline: Been using for nearly a decade
comments: I've been using this concealer for a long time and keep going back to it.  I started using it in my 40's and now I'm in my 50's. As many others have mentioned, the pump is a pain.  This has been less problematic for me because I tend to need more product (many spots to cover). I'm getting to the age where if I want something under my eyes at all I have to use a different product.  The products that don't settle tend to be less resilient , they are greasier and somehow disappear as the day wears on.  Still on the search for the ultimate concealer that does it all.  This product was probably designed for younger people who still have enough collagen that they still have bouncy, smooth skin.  For those who are older - its best used for covering noticeable spots.

headline: Pretty good - feels like a good lotion!
comments:
My first thought was that it looks quite tinted - the sunscreen is quite dark and thoroughly in the medium skin tone range. My skin is light-medium (slightly lighter than the cream) but it blended well into my skin. There's no coverage though so you'll have to use something else for that - I assume the tint is mostly to avoid a white cast when applying. 
It feels pretty light and like most other lotions and leaves my skin with a light dewy finish - I'm a little worried that it could end up shiny by the end of the day but it looks fine for now! It's supposed to be moisturizing and definitely feels like a normal moisturizing lotion (albeit tinted) so I think it does that job well. 

I've been using it on and off for the past week and while I can't really tell how well it works as sunscreen, it's pretty easy to apply and I like how well the tint blends in. 

However, the packaging/tube isn't the best - after a few uses the pump at the end of the tube wasn't working until I squeezed the rest of the tube into the pump, and I was also a little concerned whether it would make the pump expel too much. But I was careful and it worked fine and I haven't run into the issue again. 
The cap is also strange and not completely flat (it's slightly rounded) so it's not completely stable when you stand it up on its cap!

(I was offered by peterthomasroth this product for free in exchange for an honest review!)

headline: Been using for nearly a decade
comments: I've been using this concealer for a long time and keep going back to it.  I started using it in my 40's and now I'm in my 50's.  It does a great job of concealing dark spots and red acne scars all day long.  It does a better job if you let it dry for 5-10 minutes before putting on any liquid foundation. As many others have mentioned, the pump is a pain.  This has been less problematic for me because I tend to need more product (many spots to cover). What has been less helpful is that it is not great for under the eyes (if you are over 45)  and have more crows feet forming.  It tends to settle into the lines (even with primer).  I'm getting to the age where if I want something under my eyes at all I have to use a different product.  The products that don't settle tend to be less resilient , they are greasier and somehow disappear as the day wears on.  Still on the search for the ultimate concealer that does it all.  This product was probably designed for younger people who still have enough collagen that they still have bouncy, smooth skin.  For those who are older - its best used for covering noticeable spots.

headline: gets a lot right

As always, whether a product calls itself a moisturizer, foundation, or "sheer tint moisturizer" as this does, bear in mind you will need 1/4 tsp on average for face and neck to reach that SPF on the packaging. You can certainly wear that level of this without it looking or feeling off. It blends in effortlessly and feels great to wear.

However, as is the case with universal tints, I suspect this might not work for those of us on extreme ends. I am quite fair, and so when I wear the full 1/4 tsp of this, it does look off on me. Granted, not as bad as some sunscreens, but just a little off. I do think this will be perfect for light to tan skin tones though.

As many others have mentioned, the pump is a pain.  This has been less problematic for me because I tend to need more product (many spots to cover). What has been less helpful is that it is not great for under the eyes (if you are over 45)  and have more crows feet forming.  It tends to settle into the lines (even with primer).  I'm getting to the age where if I want something under my eyes at all I have to use a different product.  The products that don't settle tend to be less resilient , they are greasier and somehow disappear as the day wears on.  Still on the search for the ultimate concealer that does it all.  This product was probably designed for younger people who still have enough collagen that they still have bouncy, smooth skin.  For those who are older - its best used for covering noticeable spots.

I have to be carefully blend it out & cover it well with my other concealer but it does brighten them much more than concealer alone. If I don't cover enough it does look weirdly bright yellow. I probably end up wasting product though doing it this way but it works better. I'm going to get the pink & see if that matches my skin tone better so that's the only thing I'd be aware of & why I didn't give it 5 stars. I have a wonderful pot concealer from NYX but I have to use a brush with it. I was looking for something with the same type coverage but easier to put on. headline: Purchased myself at Ulta
comments:

It has a skin-like finish that doesn't look cakey or obvious and performs beautifully both under the eyes and as a spot concealer. The lightest shade, 0.5N, has a truly neutral undertone, is a great skintone match for me (MAC NW10) and thankfully, doesn't contain any shimmer or sparkles. I find it applies best with a sponge (dry or damp), which prevents it from clinging to dry patches, and while powder will increase the wear time, it's not necessary as this is self setting. I've been on the hunt for a new concealer ever since Dior's Forever Skin Correct was ruined by reformulation and so far, this has been a great replacement.

headline: Not "creamy" OR radiant
comments: Searched for ages for a creamy hydrating concealer for post-menopausal skin, that does not settle into fine lines or wrinkles or feel dry. This had best reviews so I ordered before a trip from Ulta, so I was stuck using it on my trip and afterwards didnt get it returned in time unfortunately. Wondering if I got an old one, b/c it was NOT creamy or radiant, it was dry, hard to blend, looked heavy and cakey. Giving it two stars b/c I heard great things and was really hopeful, but the quality for me was one star. Ive used it b/c it was expensive, but started blending it on the back of my hand with just a tiny bit of good eye cream, and used a soft concealer brush to apply mainly in and under inner corners of eye and at outer corners to brighten. Worked ok, def better WITH the eye cream. But has to be set with powder, which is a "maturing skin" nightmare. I DID NOT use it underneath my entire eye area, it was just too dry and heavy/cakey, and enhanced fine lines and wrinkles and crepey-ness of delicate under eye area. It lasted FOREVER so I was stuck with it for quite some time. I'm just now running out of it - thank goodness, but i suppose the search is on again. :/ Concealer is so difficult to find for aging skin!

headline: Worth every penny!
comments:
I have tried so many concealers over the years, desperately seeking something that covers my dark under eye circles (genetic). Most concealers were either too light in coverage or not a good shade match. This is now my holy grail product, the unicorn I've been searching for. It offers great coverage and I find the 20.0 Medium to be a true neutral. I'd say it skews more toward light-medium since I'm not a true medium and it's perfect for me. 

For reference, the best concealer color match I've found is Smashbox's light neutral olive (it just wasn't full enough coverage for this girl's dark circles) and for foundation I wear Mineral Fusion's olive 2 in pressed powder. Basically my skin matches an olive that grew in the shade so color matches are tough.

A word about texture: if you're used to liquid concealers, this one is going to surprise you with how thick it is. You might think it's dried out. It's not! If you're used to solid/stick concealers, you'll understand it. You can only do minimal blending, so finding a good shade match will help. I use my finger to apply it using gentle taps. And if the finish is a bit too shiny for you, I find a dusting of setting powder helps give it a slightly more matte look. Also, everyone is right that a little goes a long way. I suspect one regular tube will last me more than a year, so the price is absolutely worth it.

headline: Please keep making this!

Ordered: Porcelain-Beige
