I am in my early 40's but struggle most with my undereye area. Due to an eye disease, the skin around my eyes is very thin. I have tried every technique you can think of with undereye concealer and makeup tricks to help cover my circles/undereye redness/purple veins around my eyes/bags. Everything I try just seems to make me look older.
I find that regular foundations are too thick and make my skin look more dry (even with a good skin care routine beforehand including moisturizer and primer; allowing each layer to set before going to the next). I've even researched the do's and don'ts of makeup layering, e.g. not combining water-based products with silicon-based.
I switched to concealers only and color correcting to cut down on the amount of product. Most concealers are still too thick or make my lines more prominent.
NOW THIS; the IT Bye Bye Redness is working wonders for me. I am between a 10.5 to 14 in IT shades and in Tarte I use 16N for highlight and 20B for a closer skin match. I ordered the lightest shade of this product. I agree with other reviewers that it may be too dark for very fair-skinned people as this product has a peach quality to help cancel redness. 
The product does not look heavy or make me look like I have on a load of makeup. A little goes a long way. Feels very soft on the skin and doesn't rub off like other products.

I have combo skin that's dry around my eyes and this doesn't grip to my dry patches or accentuate crepe texture. The only complaint I have is the shade range..leaves a LOT to be desired for deep skin tones and the fairest tonesâ¦I use the lighter shade and am very lucky it's a near perfect match to my skin tone, but that won't be the case for everyone. I have warm/yellow undertones and find that shade 20 + 60 is a beautiful mix. Another option is to just use the lighter shade and apply a slightly darker powder). I use the water blush in Warm Pink and my face looks hydrated, beautiful, and blemish-free all day long. Love it! I have found the One!

headline: ehhhh
comments: There's a lot to say here. I've been a HUGE fan of MAC foundation and have used them exclusively for at least 10 years. My all time favorite was the Nourishing Waterproof, followed by Studio Fix Fluid. When MAC discontinued the Nourishing Waterproof foundation, I switched back to SFF only to find nearly all of the shades out of stock for the last several months. After chatting with a MAC artist, I was advised that this product is the same formula as the Nourishing Waterproof. I have SEVERAL issues with that statement. 1. No. It isn't. I don't know what is different, but this formula is far thinner and nowhere near as long lasting or full coverage as Nourishing Waterproof. --AND -- 2. It's a fraction of the size for substantially more money. The packaging is hideous, I have accidentally squeezed out foundation more times than I can count trying to recap the "pen." I don't understand the "pen" part, since that seems to be a completely useless application for this product. It's just a real disappointment both in the value for the money and the suggestion that this is anything like the original Nourishing Waterproof. Sadly, with SFF being so difficult to find online or in stores, I'll be looking away from MAC for foundation now. MAC - if you can alienate me, you're in trouble. I've been with you forever, please bring back foundation that is worth the time and money. This isn't it.

headline: Worth the price & covers blemishes & acne marks.
comments: I received this powder concealer from my mother in law last year. As time has gone on my acne, and now red spots from old acne have taken over my face. What makes it even more difficult is I actually sell skincare and makeup. I personally do my skin care, primer, CC cream, liquid foundation, and THEN I use this concealer on any recent blemish/pimple/acne marks peeling through. And let me tell you it works amazing! I feel much more confident using this, as I've went 34 years without severe acne (just got on a prescription ointment)! I recently told my mother in law I ran out and she just brought me another container.  I will say I have fine lines under my eyes and don't prefer to Usenet for that, hence why I said I use liquid. Sometimes I'll use on my eye lids alone, or as a primer, as well as for redness around my nose. But what I do know is it covers any blemishes and red marks/scars helping me not feel like whoever I come in contact with is staring at my acne/red marks. Don't forget: a little goes a LONG way. You need the tiniest amount put into the cap, then onto the blur brush, tap, and straight to the skin. If it looks super caked on I consider the following: is my skin moisturized enough? Did I forget my primer? Did I to use a setting spray? Did I apply to much? Serious very pigmented so only use a a tiny amount specifically with the blurring brush and you should have great results (I've sold skincare and makeup for several different companies, all that either met or exceeded EU standards and this takes the cake by far). My mother in law has said sometimes she will simple use her finger to apply to a tiny blemished area, but I've never tried it as the blurring brush is top notch IMO.

headline: try before buying full size
comments:
I use the shape tape concealer to cut a crease and clean up small areas like winged liner/shadow and flaws around my lips when wearing bold lipstick bc thats easier than trying to rub it off and having smear all over my face. 

I find this concealer to be the best for cutting creases and creating negative space with eye looks. I'm 44 with dry skin so I stopped wearing complexion products years ago. I do a lot of bold and smoky eye looks and always use glitter or shimmery shades (I highly recommend trying some liquid shadows if you look bold and blingy looks without having glitter all over your face) that tend to land under my eyes during application, brushes will always fling the glitter everywhere. I'll use A wipe to clean it up around my eyes but if I don't have any handy I'll just tap a tiny dot of this to cover the mess. when not using this, I'll tap a light eye shadow or cream shadow/highlight shade with my finger. if you've learned contouring watching yt or ig tutorials where they pour concealer all over around the eyes-- keep in mind it may be necessary for photoshoots, theatrical performers, people under set lighting in front of cameras, but not necessary for the average person. it's wayyy too much product and will cake up, crease, and accentuate dry skin and fine lines like a magnifying glass. then putting powder or baking will make it worse no matter which brand you use. matte complexion products shouldn't be used on dry skin or mature skin. tinted moisturizers, creams, and Dewey products work better.

if you're having problems with creasing, caking, and dryness with this concealer- you're probably using too much product. try putting a small dollup on the back of your hand and use a finger to tap it on pressing it in or using a smaller brush besides the applicator. 

you can also add a little of a moisurizer mixed on your hand then applied to keep it from drying out your skin.

headline: try before buying full size
comments:
I use the shape tape concealer to cut a crease and clean up small areas like winged liner/shadow and flaws around my lips when wearing bold lipstick bc thats easier than trying to rub it off and having smear all over my face. 

I find this concealer to be the best for cutting creases and creating negative space with eye looks. I'm 44 with dry skin so I stopped wearing complexion products years ago. I do a lot of bold and smoky eye looks and always use glitter or shimmery shades (I highly recommend trying some liquid shadows if you look bold and blingy looks without having glitter all over your face) that tend to land under my eyes during application, brushes will always fling the glitter everywhere. I'll use A wipe to clean it up around my eyes but if I don't have any handy I'll just tap a tiny dot of this to cover the mess. when not using this, I'll tap a light eye shadow or cream shadow/highlight shade with my finger. if you've learned contouring watching yt or ig tutorials where they pour concealer all over around the eyes-- keep in mind it may be necessary for photoshoots, theatrical performers, people under set lighting in front of cameras, but not necessary for the average person. it's wayyy too much product and will cake up, crease, and accentuate dry skin and fine lines like a magnifying glass. then putting powder or baking will make it worse no matter which brand you use. matte complexion products shouldn't be used on dry skin or mature skin. tinted moisturizers, creams, and Dewey products work better.

if you're having problems with creasing, caking, and dryness with this concealer- you're probably using too much product. try putting a small dollup on the back of your hand and use a finger to tap it on pressing it in or using a smaller brush besides the applicator. 

you can also add a little of a moisurizer mixed on your hand then applied to keep it from drying out your skin.

My eye was so so purple, and I'm not even joking when I say my coworkers couldn't even really tell that I had much of a bruise at all; they had to stare really intently to see anything. This stuff is kind of magic and really saved me a lot of embarrassment. I would definitely recommend it!!!

headline: Holy grail for aging skin, dark circles, if applied right
comments: I have thin, pale skin and deep set eyes, so my undereye is perpetually a dark purple that's nearly impossible to cover up. On top of that, I'm in my 30s and my skin is getting dry, plus fine lines are starting. Most full coverage concealers settle into those fine lines no matter what I do. Not this one - with caveats: First - don't apply it thick like beauty youtubers.  When I say a little goes a long way I am serious.  I got the best results by applying 10 minutes after my normal skincare on moisturized skin, no primer, in a TINY dot on the darkest part of my undereye, then blended out by tapping my fingers. This stuff is THICK and did not spread well with beauty blenders or brushes, and looks a hot mess if you apply it heavy. However, it looked perfectly smooth when applied extremely light and blended with my fingers. After it completely dries, I will layer if I need more coverage - which I don't. This is truly full coverage.  Second, skip the setting powder unless you have VERY oily skin. Like extra oily - my eye lids are naturally oily and I still didn't need to set this concealer. This stuff dries down matte and setting powder makes the drying worse, causing it to flake and emphasize fine lines. Using this method, the result looked like my natural skin, absolutely no caking, settling, or flaking, and it stayed put all day.

headline: Surprisingly good
comments: I picked this up on a whim in the shade 03 because I wanted to try a stick concealer and this is a brand I hadn't used before. I am pleasantly surprised by how smooth the formula is, and how natural this looks. I previously only used cream and liquid concealers, but after using this stick I actually prefer the application of this one. It's not the heaviest coverage - more like light buildable natural coverage, but it pairs well with my tinted moisturizer and liquid foundation, and even looks good on it's own. On my worst areas (under eyes, crease around my nostrils, old breakouts) it actually looks decent and doesn't crease, cake or dry out terribly. If you are looking for a more natural coverage and a thin formula that isn't super greasy and doesn't dry down to a matte finish, you may really like this product. My one issue is that it's not easy finding a shade both due to the lack of pictures on the website and because people hardly ever talk about this brand on YouTube - usually my go-to for shade matching. 03 seems to be perfect for my light/med golden skin tone.

headline: Great silicone based primer
comments:
This is an amazing skin perfecting primer, it's a lightweight, oil free, & velvety smooth primer.
It's a clear gel formula that melts on contact with skin. It helps to erase pores and smooth out lines and uneven texture. I use a pea sized amount, rub it between my fingers warming it up. And then I use rubbing and tapping motions to apply. It helps to make your makeup go on easily, stay fresh, and last longer.
It's a silicone based formula and I love using it when I want my makeup to last all day & you can also wear it alone too. I little goes a long way, you really can stretch this formula to cover more of your skin. It's an antioxidant blend with vitamins A&E, grapeseed extract, and green tea. Im a big fan of this primer and I think if you try it yourself you will see why Its their number one selling primer.

headline: It's great
comments: You have to wait till your skin care absorbs THEN apply this primer. A little goes along way. Make sure you wait MORE than 15 seconds for the primer to set, I wait a full minute. I don't recommend buffing foundation because it can disrupt the primer which can cause piling, so I use a flat kabuki or flat angled to apply my foundation. Also there is some trial and error to see what kind of foundation works with this primer. Anyway I am not sure why I don't try this primer sooner, maybe because back then I believed how bad silicones are for acne when it isn't the case for me. This primer helps keep my face moisturized due to how occlusive it is. It also helps create that barrier to keep my foundation from breaking when I get oily. I am super oily and this primer has helped to make me feel like I have normal skin. Even my under eye concealer doesn't crack. I've used this primer with the LM Real Flawless and several Korean BB creams that are more on the thicker consistency. I've also used this with just powder over it.

headline: Great silicone based primer
comments:
This is an amazing skin perfecting primer, it's a lightweight, oil free, & velvety smooth primer.
It's a clear gel formula that melts on contact with skin. It helps to erase pores and smooth out lines and uneven texture. I use a pea sized amount, rub it between my fingers warming it up. And then I use rubbing and tapping motions to apply. It helps to make your makeup go on easily, stay fresh, and last longer.
It's a silicone based formula and I love using it when I want my makeup to last all day & you can also wear it alone too. I little goes a long way, you really can stretch this formula to cover more of your skin. It's an antioxidant blend with vitamins A&E, grapeseed extract, and green tea. Im a big fan of this primer and I think if you try it yourself you will see why Its their number one selling primer.

headline: It's great
comments: You have to wait till your skin care absorbs THEN apply this primer. A little goes along way. Make sure you wait MORE than 15 seconds for the primer to set, I wait a full minute. I don't recommend buffing foundation because it can disrupt the primer which can cause piling, so I use a flat kabuki or flat angled to apply my foundation. Also there is some trial and error to see what kind of foundation works with this primer. Anyway I am not sure why I don't try this primer sooner, maybe because back then I believed how bad silicones are for acne when it isn't the case for me. This primer helps keep my face moisturized due to how occlusive it is. It also helps create that barrier to keep my foundation from breaking when I get oily. I am super oily and this primer has helped to make me feel like I have normal skin. Even my under eye concealer doesn't crack. I've used this primer with the LM Real Flawless and several Korean BB creams that are more on the thicker consistency. I've also used this with just powder over it.

headline: Great silicone based primer
comments:
This is an amazing skin perfecting primer, it's a lightweight, oil free, & velvety smooth primer.
It's a clear gel formula that melts on contact with skin. It helps to erase pores and smooth out lines and uneven texture. I use a pea sized amount, rub it between my fingers warming it up. And then I use rubbing and tapping motions to apply. It helps to make your makeup go on easily, stay fresh, and last longer.
It's a silicone based formula and I love using it when I want my makeup to last all day & you can also wear it alone too. I little goes a long way, you really can stretch this formula to cover more of your skin. It's an antioxidant blend with vitamins A&E, grapeseed extract, and green tea. Im a big fan of this primer and I think if you try it yourself you will see why Its their number one selling primer.

headline: It's great
comments: You have to wait till your skin care absorbs THEN apply this primer. A little goes along way. Make sure you wait MORE than 15 seconds for the primer to set, I wait a full minute. I don't recommend buffing foundation because it can disrupt the primer which can cause piling, so I use a flat kabuki or flat angled to apply my foundation. Also there is some trial and error to see what kind of foundation works with this primer. Anyway I am not sure why I don't try this primer sooner, maybe because back then I believed how bad silicones are for acne when it isn't the case for me. This primer helps keep my face moisturized due to how occlusive it is. It also helps create that barrier to keep my foundation from breaking when I get oily. I am super oily and this primer has helped to make me feel like I have normal skin. Even my under eye concealer doesn't crack. I've used this primer with the LM Real Flawless and several Korean BB creams that are more on the thicker consistency. I've also used this with just powder over it.

headline: Not for sensitive acne/cyst prone people
comments:
This had all the ingredients I wanted but broke me out in FOUR cystic acne spots. 

I bought this because I'm oily and wanted a primer, spf, and moisturizer in one. This has bentonite clay which is good for oily skin. 

The first time I used it the pump shot the liquid straight out. Very bad pump as others mentioned. But I don't care if a pump doesn't work as long as the product does. The texture is very liquid, and maybe it's just cause I knew it had clay in it but it almost felt like watery clay water. Dried down very fast, felt like I put nothing on which is the feeling I love. Texture and pump issues aside I used it for a month.

I wanted to see my skin turn beautiful and healthy but it just started itching by the end of every day. Didn't control oil any more than my previous spf moisturizer. Then the bumps came. I ignored the first two but when the other two were coming in I knew it was time to stop using it. 

Once I stopped, the bumps started to hurt less shrink back down. It's been a month later now even though the bumps healed, the cystic acne discoloration spots are still there. So be VERY careful if you are prone to cystic acne.

Paulas choice matte spf 30 is the best I've found. But I wanted to try something different. Oh well.

headline: A game changer!

headline: Not worth it at that price point
comments:

I'm no stranger to primers and highlighters so this product was certainly within my wheelhouse. The packaging of the product itself is beautiful; the light pink ombrÃ© tube is a complement to the primer itself, illustrating the ethereal and slightly pinkish glow of the product. I did also notice that my skin felt tacky after application but that's pretty standard for me  with most primers and highlighters I've tried. 

Overall, this might be decent for someone looking for a moderate highlighter and not needing it for foundation priming. Unfortunately not one of the better LM products I've tried and certainly not at that price point.

headline: This really is a hero! I don't ever want to be without it!
comments: I ignored this product ever since it came out and didn't think it was something I really needed. Then I got a sample and WHOA! I don't ever want to be without it. This stuff is the real deal!  At first I became interested because it just felt so good on my face, so I ordered a small tube and used it for several days. A few weeks before I got the sample, I had gotten a pimple for the first time in literally YEARS (I'm in my 50s) and it was one of those that wound up scarring somewhat, and it was one of those spots that looked like it might not go away and was in a VERY visible place on my lower cheek near my mouth. I really wasn't much into skin care until the last few years when I started trying to take better care of my skin, so I was really upset about this new spot.  After a week or so, it seemed to have faded. After a few weeks now? That spot is barely there at all! I am 110% a believer in Skin Hero now! It just feels really nice, no scent to me, and the skin on my face just feels softer, better, and definitely looks better. It just feels like it's really doing something and working!  I'm using CC Red Correct (which I also ignored for a while ; thought I didn't need since I don't have rosacea or a lot of redness) after Skin Hero - turns out after 2 years of using CC Cream in Clair, the CC Red Correct shade is MUCH better suited to my extremely fair skin ; blonde hair - now, between Skin Hero helping fade the new spot that was bothering me and it + CC Red Correct basically covering up all of my imperfections (some veins around my nose and a few other red spots here and there) - my face has never looked better! I prefer to go without makeup most days ; don't really need it but occasionally, and now with CC Red Correct + Skin Hero, I am fine with skipping makeup most of the time. They are both just THAT good!  Skin Hero + CC Red Correct are also even helping with my hereditary dark circles under my eyes, which there's realistically no real cure for. Are they still there? Yes. Do they look better? DEFINITELY!  I have used the BB ; CC Creams in Clair for over 2 years now and have stopped using foundation entirely, but I really wish I'd discovered the CC Red Correct first before the CC Cream in Clair! And now with Skin Hero + CC Red Correct, I expect I will still layer BB Cream in Clair on top on the rare times when I'm going out and want to have a little more coverage, but Skin Hero + CC Red Correct are now my go-to every single day team, and I don't ever want to have to go without either of them.   If you have been on the fence about trying Skin Hero - and I get it, I honestly didn't think I needed it or would be interested, pretty much ever since Erborian came out with it - I urge you to get a sample or small tube of Skin Hero and try it and see! I seriously do not ever want to be without it ever again now!

headline: This is a no.

Why package only 0.47 of an ounce in a container this large with only a small center tube containing the product? I literally used it a few times a week for a month and it was gone.  When it stopped pumping product I opened it thinking it was plugged. Nope. A tube less than 1/2 inch across and 7/8 inch deep was the only reservoir for the product. If I could, I would be the spokeswoman for this primer. After you read this, I think you'll agree lol. It's actually like a suit of armor for your makeup! It gives your skin a smooth, blurred, flawless look and feel (even if you don't wear makeup!). I have the most problematic skin; sensitive, textured, fine lines, big pores, acne prone, sweaty, sometimes oily, sometimes dry, sometimes combo - if you can imagine such a thing.

I've struggled for about a decade to find the right combination of products for flawless makeup. And I was a manager at Ulta, so that's how you know I've tried everything - prestige and drugstore. I must say that this is the end all, be all!

As long as I use this, just about ANY makeup I use will not separate, cake, sweat off, get patchy, or emphasize pores or texture. It just makes me look absolutely flawless from early morning into the late night! And with how troubled my skin actually is, that's truly saying something.

I swear there's nothing like it out there, it really is, quite literally, impossible! And for the price, you can't beat it. Plus, it's silicone-free, so you can feel better about putting it on your skin vs other primers. Give it a try, I'm positive you'll love it too!! < 3

headline: Works pergectly for me
comments:
I have oily acneic skin, large pores, scars and using a combination of this primer + the green glass skin has improved the look of my skin when wearing without makeup, as well as helped a ton with the smooth application of makeup especially over scars (indentations), pores, cystic acne and slicker areas like t zone, and deeper wrinkles. 

I love how it works but doesn't have that icky slippery feeling of some pore primers and it really stays on and helps prolong my makeup wear. It's thicker like a blur primer but feels lighter and more comfortable while being blendable. No pilling for me.

This is my favorite primer ever alongside the green glass correct and they work incredibly together (the Impossible helps fill and smooth over lines, pores, oily areas and acne in select areas while the green brings back a healthy dewey look and mild color correction where I need it) please please keep making them! 
Highly recommend. Very happy. Give it a chance and play around with it.

headline: This really is a hero! I don't ever want to be without it!
comments: I ignored this product ever since it came out and didn't think it was something I really needed. Then I got a sample and WHOA! I don't ever want to be without it. This stuff is the real deal!  At first I became interested because it just felt so good on my face, so I ordered a small tube and used it for several days. A few weeks before I got the sample, I had gotten a pimple for the first time in literally YEARS (I'm in my 50s) and it was one of those that wound up scarring somewhat, and it was one of those spots that looked like it might not go away and was in a VERY visible place on my lower cheek near my mouth. I really wasn't much into skin care until the last few years when I started trying to take better care of my skin, so I was really upset about this new spot.  After a week or so, it seemed to have faded. After a few weeks now? That spot is barely there at all! I am 110% a believer in Skin Hero now! It just feels really nice, no scent to me, and the skin on my face just feels softer, better, and definitely looks better. It just feels like it's really doing something and working!  I'm using CC Red Correct (which I also ignored for a while ; thought I didn't need since I don't have rosacea or a lot of redness) after Skin Hero - turns out after 2 years of using CC Cream in Clair, the CC Red Correct shade is MUCH better suited to my extremely fair skin ; blonde hair - now, between Skin Hero helping fade the new spot that was bothering me and it + CC Red Correct basically covering up all of my imperfections (some veins around my nose and a few other red spots here and there) - my face has never looked better! I prefer to go without makeup most days ; don't really need it but occasionally, and now with CC Red Correct + Skin Hero, I am fine with skipping makeup most of the time. They are both just THAT good!  Skin Hero + CC Red Correct are also even helping with my hereditary dark circles under my eyes, which there's realistically no real cure for. Are they still there? Yes. Do they look better? DEFINITELY!  I have used the BB ; CC Creams in Clair for over 2 years now and have stopped using foundation entirely, but I really wish I'd discovered the CC Red Correct first before the CC Cream in Clair! And now with Skin Hero + CC Red Correct, I expect I will still layer BB Cream in Clair on top on the rare times when I'm going out and want to have a little more coverage, but Skin Hero + CC Red Correct are now my go-to every single day team, and I don't ever want to have to go without either of them.   If you have been on the fence about trying Skin Hero - and I get it, I honestly didn't think I needed it or would be interested, pretty much ever since Erborian came out with it - I urge you to get a sample or small tube of Skin Hero and try it and see! I seriously do not ever want to be without it ever again now!

headline: Best primer I've used for very oily skin
comments: This is the first primer I've ever used that actually works for my very oily skin, but it did take some trial and error to figure it out. The best way for me to use it is to pat it on my face, and immediately apply my foundation. I use a damp sponge and apply quickly, avoiding continuously hitting the same area. Once it starts to dry, if you continue to go over the same area, or try to add more foundation, it will pill and completely pull off in little clumps. I let everything dry down completely, than finish my routine. I only get the smallest amount of shine on my nose by the end of my day, where my makeup used to nearly melt off my face before. It's definitely extra work, but if you've struggled with the frustration of very oily skin your whole life I really think you should give this a shot. I can't stress enough how happy I am to have found this and how much it has helped my confidence battling my oily face.

headline: Best primer I've used for very oily skin
comments: This is the first primer I've ever used that actually works for my very oily skin, but it did take some trial and error to figure it out. The best way for me to use it is to pat it on my face, and immediately apply my foundation. I use a damp sponge and apply quickly, avoiding continuously hitting the same area. Once it starts to dry, if you continue to go over the same area, or try to add more foundation, it will pill and completely pull off in little clumps. I let everything dry down completely, than finish my routine. I only get the smallest amount of shine on my nose by the end of my day, where my makeup used to nearly melt off my face before. It's definitely extra work, but if you've struggled with the frustration of very oily skin your whole life I really think you should give this a shot. I can't stress enough how happy I am to have found this and how much it has helped my confidence battling my oily face.

I have used other age-defying makeup, and I've been a fan of CoverGirl's Olay Simply Ageless (which I also love) for a few years. Both help with fine lines, and both offer radiance, but the Flower Beauty regimen, I described above, is now my go-to. I don't wear full makeup every single day, but when I do, this elixir and the Light Illusion Foundation make me glow and look fresh, clean, and seriously younger. Just this week, my coworker remarked how great my skin looks lately, and I attribute it to my pore vacuum and Flower Beauty products. If you are going to try the elixir, I recommend reading about how best to utilize it. Yes; you can wear it on its own, but it won't soak in right away. You have to give it a little time to do so. Apply it sparingly, because it goes a long way. I use a drop the size of a dime to cover my entire face in a generous but thin layer, and I still end up washing a bit off my hands when I'm done. It spreads out beautifully. Using too much will absolutely give you a greasy, slippery face, as some reviewers have described. When I wear the elixir, without makeup, I do the retinol, wait a few minutes, and then apply the elixir in a thin layer. After that, I don't touch my face again. I love this product and hope it's available for a long time to come!

I can not rave enough about the compliments I received after using this primer in my makeup routine. I recommend Dermablend's brilliant base illuminating primer to anyone searching for a healthier and professional primer that leaves your face radiant and beautiful. 

Thanks to Dermablend for sending me this free sample to test through the BzzAgent sampling program.

headline: Still Loving
comments:
To preface, I love and have a soft spot for essence products. I wrote a review of this product 3 months ago and I'm still loving it just as much. I use it maybe 3 times a week and there's still plenty of product in there 3 months later (to be fair, i don't use a whole lot and mostly focus on my tzone, but try to cover my whole face). I've used it with mineral sunscreen, chemical sunscreen, water-based foundations, silicone-based foundations, you name it - and it's never once pilled. It gives any foundation such a smooth surface to work with and I get such joy out of gliding foundation over it. Others have mentioned a fragrance - it's so light that i barely notice it, and i have sensitive skin and it doesn't affect me, but I agree it does have a slight fragrance (although I didn't even realize it had a fragrance until I read other reviews). A lot of products make me break out, but this one never has. It's also not drying, and even though it says it's matte, I can still achieve a nice glow if I want to depending on what products I put on top of it. 
Overall it's just a lovely smooth and blurring canvas for makeup, as it says it is. It's my favorite primer I've ever used and I use it far more often than a similarly mattifying silicone-based high end primer that I'm trying to use up.

headline: Still Loving

I've used it with mineral sunscreen, chemical sunscreen, water-based foundations, silicone-based foundations, you name it - and it's never once pilled. It gives any foundation such a smooth surface to work with and I get such joy out of gliding foundation over it. Others have mentioned a fragrance - it's so light that i barely notice it, and i have sensitive skin and it doesn't affect me, but I agree it does have a slight fragrance (although I didn't even realize it had a fragrance until I read other reviews). A lot of products make me break out, but this one never has. It's also not drying, and even though it says it's matte, I can still achieve a nice glow if I want to depending on what products I put on top of it. 
Overall it's just a lovely smooth and blurring canvas for makeup, as it says it is. It's my favorite primer I've ever used and I use it far more often than a similarly mattifying silicone-based high end primer that I'm trying to use up.

headline: *HAD* to try this one, I'm glad I did!!
comments:
This primer goes on very smooth and leaves your face ready for makeup. I do my skincare, and to then have my makeup only last a few hours is a bummer.
That's not the case with this one!

I used to mix paint and learned the primer was the "glue" to keep paint in place. If you didn't paint shortly after, you would have to prime again.

I have tried a lot of primers and find it tricky to get the right one. It can't be for oily skin or have mica particles. I just want a great primer made with good ingredients.
I have fair, dry, sensitive skin with tendencies to redness.

This primer was perfectly tolerated by my skin. It's what I'm currently using!

I sort of adapted that with my skincare and makeuo, and I've learned not all primers are created equal.
I finish foundation by stippling to make it smooth. This primer has that "grip" to keep my makeup in place. It lasted a full day, 9+ hours!

My suggestion is to tap primer lightly on your skin after applying, giving it a few minutes to smooth before applying your makeup.

headline: Lightweight primer with skincare benefits
comments: *I received this product for free as part of a campaign*. This primer claims to plump up dry skin, be safe for sensitive skin, and be made from lightweight breathable formulas. My skin tends to go from oily to dry depending one the weather. I applied this primer as instructed; Apply 1-2 pumps to clean fingertips and massage into skin. Let the formula set for one minute to absorb and activate. The texture is lightweight, as it's drying it's sticky, but it doesn't stay sticky. I then applied foundation as usual. I think overall, it did a good job as a primer. It filled in my pores well. I like how this product contains skincare, so the more you wear it, the better the effects. If you look at the ingredients, they do all promote hydration. I didn't notice too much of a difference in my skin texture, however I liked it because it didn't break me out. One thing I didn't like was the packaging, the pump didn't always dispense product.

I will be purchasing more colors and keeping this as my new travel blush. The squeeze tube is about the size of a lip balm and the packaging is cute too. This is very multi-use. You can use it as blush, eyeshadow, or a subtle lip stain. An absolute steal for the price. You could probably compare this to the Laneige Glowy Makeup Serum. This is definitely a product you want to let sink in for a few minutes before applying makeup, and a little does go a long way. I'm surprised by how lightweight and oily it is because it hasn't caused any separation for me yet. 

The glow this gives is otherworldlyâa true glass skin product. This is a product that will instantly illuminate any complexion product.

headline: Undone primer oil
comments: I wasn't sure about thus product at first, but I was pleasantly surprised. It starts off oily, then thins out and sinks into the skin. I have combo skin and it didn't look greasy, just hydrated and fresh. Unique product...recommended.

headline: Amazing for minimizing grayness
comments: I'm South Asian and have grayness around my mouth area. A light layer of this product makes a huge difference in how my foundation looks. It's not so pigmented that you have to apply it carefully, but it's pigmented enough that it actually makes a difference. It doesn't change the formula of any of my foundations and concealers in my experience. If you have a medium skintone or deeper you'll find this very useful. As someone with a deeper skintone I know it's frustrating when a product only available in one shade doesn't work for you, so I hope L'Oreal comes out with a version for lighter skintones. I hope the negative reviews from people with lighter skintones don't cause them to discontinue this product.

headline: Definitely works/Great for oily tan or deep tones

headline: Use for dark circles

headline: A More Refined You
comments: Labeled as Ã¢â¬Ëmakeup with skin care', Skin Hero takes a more honest approach to the Ã¢â¬Åno pigment foundationÃ¢â¬Â idea.    As someone who doesn't often wear foundation/base, I use this product in its place.  Skin Hero acts as a primer and perfects the complexion, but it lacks the silky slip of silicones in the Pink Primer & Care. I do not find this formula particularly hydrating, but it's not drying either.    The consistency is a thick, but lightweight gel-cream.  The color is a very pale greenish cream (like the lightest shade of Jade), and it helps to subtly color correct minor redness.  It gently mattifies, without making skin appear dull; it blurs pores, giving a soft focus effect on the skin, and it wears nicely throughout the day.    My only criticism of Skin Hero is that it's not very smooth in terms of application. It's not buildableÃ¢â¬" if you try to build up coverage, you'll see powdery greenish cream colored streaks on your face.    I have found that I negate this the best by applying the product as I would a foundation. I use my fingers, and gently spread a small amount of product, then pat it in.    I see the subtle difference it makes on my complexion without tint. It really does perfect, and I really like that!

headline: I use it different but LOVE IT!
comments:
I love this stuff! I don't know if I wear it as intended however the results I get are FANTASTIC! To start... I am 43 yrs old with very dry skin. I have redness across my nose & cheeks. I have wrinkles between my eyebrows (the 11) on the corners of my mouth & 3-4 surprised lines on my forehead over my eyebrows. I also have fine lines around my eyes, which intensify if my skin is really dry. I find myself absolutely needing to exfoliate 2-3 times a week to control the flaky pealing skin look. 
Ok, with that said, if you're in the same general situation, you have to try this! 
After my serum, moisturizer, & tiny bit of foundation soak in. I take my ring finger and twirl it around to pick up product & rub my ring fingers together to warm it up. I then dab it under my eyes continuously to the outside upwards towards the brow & right under the brow. I continue dabbing until I've worked it over the 11 wrinkles between my eyebrows,& then dab back to where I started. This has a matting effect & also softens wrinkles excellently. It is a slick product but has a drying matte finish. I only use this product on areas which I do NOT apply setting powder. I used to but this is a replacement for a matte finish setting powder. It did not blend with my powder but it might with a different brand. I use Laura's translucent loose. I like this look much more than the powder finish. It's a finishing product for me, not a primer. headline: Great product, easy to over-apply if you have fair skin
comments:
This stuff is REALLY pigmented, which is a double-edged sword if you have lighter skin. (I have very fair skin and bought the shade "Soft Tulip.") On one hand, I love the color and dewy glow, and one bottle is going to last me a very long time! On the other hand, it's easy to over-apply if you use it straight out of the bottle with the provided applicator. 

Here's a tip if you have light skin: pull out the applicator, dab a *tiny* amount on to your finger, and blend that in across your cheekbone in a circular motion. If that's still too much, take a dry beauty blender and dab dab dab to remove the excess. It takes a bit of practice but you can definitely make this product work on fair skin.

headline: Cool packaging and formula just not my shade
comments: This is the shade BABY PINK it's definitely pigmented and vibrant as you can see from the photos. I think the color on the package that is advertised it a bit more muted pink and this is a very bright almost purple pink that isn't very flattering even on my light skin tone. I don't think it would work for many skin tones at all. It feels hydrating when applied and the applicator is awesome because you can determine how much you squeeze out and where you want to apply. I like to apply to my hand then use a brush to apply serum blush but you could put this directly on your cheek if you wish. It does grip to the skin and dry down matte but definitely seeps into pores and looks a bit patchy. It's vegan and good for 12 months after opening. The formula has a gel like texture, and has niacinamide and pomegranate peels extract for moisture, high coverage and blurred finish. Overall I think it's an innovative product package and formula and the matte effect is impressive from a liquid blush, but this particular color is a bit too vibrant and I didn't like the patchiness when applied to my skin.

headline: Easily blendable & very pigmented
comments:
I can be a bit picky when it comes to blushes, but this blush really surprised me!! I have tried quite a few liquid blushes and found that they often came across patchy and have stuck with the elf putty blushes for the last few years (which I loveeee). 
I found this blush to be very easy to blend, nicely pigmented, and it has a very nice texture (on the thinner side which I love). In contrast to the popular charlotte tilbury blush which has the spongy like applicator, this blush has a squeezey precision applicator. I found this to be wayyyy more sanitary and you have a lot of control over how much product comes out (which helps prevent too much blush from coming out). 
I took 1 star off for 2 reasons;
- while easily blendable, it can come across patchy if you don't properly blend and/or use too much so just beware 
- I didn't love the color selection. I received a bright pink-like color (which I don't really love), but that's a personal preference

headline: LOVE the Color, a Bit Hard to Blend
comments:
I received this product for free from Anastasia Beverly Hills for an honest review. 

Qualities: This is a serum blush with a matte finish. It also has no smell, or at least one that is not bothersome enough for me to be able to smell it. 

Pros: I love the packaging on this, as the dropper style makes it so much easier to take only a small amount (as you only need a small amount!). It is great on bare skin to give a flush look and can be applied with your fingers if on bare skin. It is also highly pigmented, which is why you need so little! Once it is on, it is ON! It will withstand rubs, sweat, and oils pretty well. 

Cons: It dries down very fast and can be hard to blend without pulling up your foundation. I have tried it with my fingers, a sponge, and a brush and have the most success with a brush. I place a dot on the back of my hand and dip my bristles in it and then blend it onto my cheeks that way! 

Overall: Although it is not perfect, I do enjoy the color so much I will keep using it! Once I figured out the best method for me, it has become great to use!

I received this product for free from Morphe and Bzzagent in exchange for an honest review.

The formula is almost like a gel-liquid hybrid, very easy to blend and gives a lovely natural finish. I did encounter some patchiness when using over powder products, but I don't expect most of my cream or liquid formulas to play nicely over powders anyway, so this wasn't a huge issue for me. I do think this blush formula works best with minimal makeup underneath as it blends to a really juicy fresh finish (see my picture). Packaging is nice and compact, and the squeeze applicator makes it easy to apply just a bit and not waste product. Overall a great pick!

headline: How I use the shades is a bit different
comments: I love this blush. The shades have a pretty consistent formula and texture, which isnt always the case with liquid blush. I use shades pink and buffed peach as blush, and raspberry with a teeeny bit of a live tinted stick to contour. I have very fair skin (especially in the summer time) so i like to do contour with tones that are a bit more mauve. A painter once told me that face shadows are actually very blue and purple, and that stuck with me. I feel like a cool-toned dark purple is actually the best shade for me to use to contour versus something more brown. Buffed peach is very sheer, so i use a dot of it along with pink to help sheer it out and hydrate my skin. I set it with either rare beauty or nars blush and it lasts all day. I usually use a face oil and the youthforia primer to prime, fenty foundation, nars concealer, laura mercier setting powder, and urban decay setting spray. I'm a cheer/gymnastics coach and sometimes work 11-hour days in the summer heat, and this combo holds up well for that entire time. For reference, i use a generous dot of each and a real techniques brush to blend it all together. I apply powder blush on top of it to set it so it has more staying power.

headline: Watercolor flush
comments:
This is an exceptionally pretty product that I initially wrote off. So glad I tried it again. I now have Light Pink, Warm Pink, and Peach, and at least one of those is in daily use. While this is a product I would call "sheer", it is not like a typical unpigmented blush. There is absolutely pigment. The way it applies is like a wash of a watercolor-like flush. And each of my three light shades show up differently on the skin (very surprising for a "sheer" product). It molds to the skin and looks incredibly natural. It can easily be built up. It can be blended out after it starts to set. And it lasts all day. I've worn this over liquid and cream foundations without any issue. 

Application: my preferred method is squirting out a half, or full, pump on the back of the had and smushing it up for a sec. Doesn't need to be fully mixed if using with a brush. I pick up the blush with dense flathead brush to really press this into my skin, this will give very good color payoff. I'll also use fluffier blush or bronzer brush to pick up the product for a draped lighter flushed look (from hollows of cheeks, up and out over whole cheek area and up and around the temples and eyebrows). Then I pick up any pigment left on the back of my hand with my fingers and add or build up color where I want.

headline: Gloooowing
comments: I had my eye on Nudestix for awhile and finally pulled the trigger during the 21 Days of Beauty sale. Out of all the products I ordered, I couldn't wait to get this and try it. Let me tell you, it did not disappoint and is now a staple in my makeup. The packaging is sleek and simple. The stick comes in a small metal container that has a handy little mirror on the inside of the lid, which is helpful to use on the go and to store it in your purse, and the stick itself is in a metal tube. It's easy to hold while you apply the product and it's so creamy and glides easily over my skin. The color was absolutely amazing and gave me this gorgeous, dewy glow, making my skin look healthy and refreshed. There's a subtle shimmer that enhances the color perfectly and contributes to the glow effect. It doesnt look caked on or artificial like, "hey im wearing blush everyone!". Just a very pretty and natural finish that lasts throughout the day. Im also completely obsessed with the brush applicatorâ¦ its so soft yet firm enough to effectively and easily blend the color. I use the brush when blending the product on my cheeks, but just use my finger when using it on my lips. I havent tried it as an eyeshadow yet, but given how versatile it is, I'm sure it will also look beautiful on the lids. I definitely want to try other Nudestix products and I'm so happy I finally tried it! I also showed it to my mom and she immediately ordered a bronzer one because she liked it so much, too. A little pricey, but you can get so much use out of it!

headline: A Natural Flush
comments: I purchased the shade 07. Against my medium neutral skin, the color is a dusty pink that looks very natural, a perfect everyday color. The texture is creamy and is easy to blend- almost too easy to blend that sometimes it blends to nothing. However, it is a buildable formula that can be layered without making your cheeks look overdone. I have extremely oily skin that is also acne prone and do have textured skin (pitted acne scars) and I find the blush sits nicely with my skin. I have had no breakouts or irritation from using the product. Since I do have textured skin the creamy formula looks more natural and better in my opinion, because it blends and melts into the skin more and doesn't "sit" on my skin like how some powder formulas do. This blush is not the most long lasting on my oily skin though. I've got about 5 hours of wear time with the product but I honestly do not mind because I am used to cheek makeup not lasting on me. I don't apply the blush directly onto my face since I am acne prone but how I like to apply it is to warm the stick on the back of my hand and pick up the color with a brush or sometimes my clean fingers.

headline: Good Formula, Light on the Pigment but Buildable!
comments:
I want to start off by clarifying that I did receive this product for free in exchange for my honest review. 

This blush/lipstick has been in my daily rotation for the past 2 weeks. I am a very pale woman with neutral undertones and find that this blush is very pretty against my skin. It blends well directly on my skin, and also with a brush when I am wearing foundation. the formula is creamy but not super pigmented. 1 swipe was definitely not enough compared to some of my more pigmented blushes. 2-4 swipes was great, and you can really keep building the color up, which I like because it allows me more control over the product. I also really like the applicator for this product, I like that it comes in a stick form that I can easily clean. I did not like this product as a lipstick, it came off super easily and pilled on my lips. 

This will continue to be in my daily makeup look because I just love how buildable it is, and how the color looks on me.

headline: Love both shades
comments:
I recently tried the KVD Beauty Good Apple Blush Balm Duo and was very pleased with the results. This blush duo offers a creamy, blendable formula that applies effortlessly and provides a beautiful, natural-looking flush to the cheeks. The compact includes two complementary shades that allow for versatile looks, from a subtle glow to a more vibrant pop of color.

The balm texture is smooth and lightweight, making it easy to build up the intensity without feeling heavy or greasy. I also appreciate how well it blends into the skin, giving a seamless finish that lasts throughout the day. The shades are highly pigmented, so a little goes a long way, which is great for getting the most out of the product.

One thing to note is that while the formula works wonderfully on normal to dry skin, those with very oily skin might find it a bit too dewy. Setting it with a light powder helps, but it's something to consider depending on your skin type.

Overall, the KVD Beauty Good Apple Blush Balm Duo is an excellent choice for those looking for a versatile, high-quality cream blush. It's easy to use, looks stunning, and stays put. Four stars!

headline: 3/4 products are good, packaging meh
comments:
I've been on the hunt for a bronzer/blush/highlighter palette that is small enough to take on the go, so I was really excited about this. The TLDR of this is that I enjoy the bronzer and two blushes, but hate the highlighter.

The blushes and bronzer are all matte formulas, and then the highlighter is the Super Shock putty-cream like formula. Personally, I never liked the Super Shock formula because I prefer using brushes when doing my makeup, and none of my brushes can pick up this formula, leaving me to do it with my fingers. Okay, whatever. I can get over that. But the biggest problem that I have with this highlighter is that it is mostly GLITTER. I love a glitter highlighter now and then, but not when using an everyday palette for an everyday look. It looks so weird to have matte bronzer and blush, and then a stripe of glitter on my cheekbones. It would be fine if the highlighter was a cute shimmery color, like Lunch Money, but it's very glittery which sucks. Tbh, I bought a cheap Essence highlighter so that I could crush up the ColourPop one and transfer the Essence one into the compact so that I can actually have an all in one palette. Oh well.

However, the packaging is a bit of a miss too. Aesthetically, it looks great, but mine no longer clasps shut even though I haven't done anything like drop it. So it's probably not a great option for traveling anymore, which was why I wanted itâ¦ lol

comments:
This is the only lip product ( chapstick, lip gloss, lipstickâ¦ all of them!) that doesn't make my throat tickle when I use it on in my lips: I have the pulse color. 

I tried a brighter red color and it just does not go well on my lips but the pulse one seems thicker and I like it more. 

I do hate that I have to sharpen it so often though. And I hate that it seems to waste so much product when I sharpen it.  

Other than that though I am really happy to have at least one product that I know will stay on nice as it dries and doesn't make my lips look horrid, and doesn't make my throat feel tingly and weird. I wish I could figure out what ingredient is doing that with other lip products. It's like when any other lip product mixes with any food on my lips it interacts and my throat freaks out. Anyways, if you experience the same thing then try this pulse and see if it works for you like it does for me.

I'm really picky with my makeup because with my skin type it's hard to find stuff that actually works, looks good, and stays working and looking good. This blush is a teensy bit glittery but honestly it's not very noticeable on the skin and it doesn't bother me at all, if anything it really helps give you that nice glow I mentioned. It being a powder, I was concerned at first with my skin type, but honestly it blends in so well it's like it's a part of my skin. I love it. headline: Beautiful formula; needs more shades
comments:
First, this handy little palette definitely gets the job done and on a pretty good range of skin tones; however, more shades are needed! These powders have a luxury feel to them. Almost buttery, a little can go a very long way! That being said, if you have VERY light skin tones, you're going to want to go in with a light hand and build! On the other hand if you have dark skin tones, you're going to be able to load up your brush and apply. They do build nicely; still though too much of a good thing is too much. So while I absolutely love this concept like the many "multiple steps palettes"  out there, it's not a one size fits all. Unfortunately finding that one size fits all is extremely hard to find in this department; that's the beauty of people being different! 
In the end, it's a fantastic little palette that I'd highly recommend; especially in an MUA bag or any makeup lovers collection that could benefit from these shades. Great price for great formulas. Now let's see more and more.

headline: Keeping One But It's Not a HG Lippie
comments: I love Nudestix eye pencils and am a sucker for makeup in this form, as I find it easier to apply amd easier to travel with. I purchased the Sweet Cheeks and Kiss (and Pulse in the Gel lip) and wasnt overly impressed. In terms of color, these mattes are nice and pigmented, as you would expect for a matte. I found Sweet Cheeks to be too bright on me, so she is going back. Kiss is a great pink-nude (no rude on me!) although mine arrived witg the tip broken off, which I don't love. Both of the mattes are fairly comfortable on although they never fully dry down so expect a bit of tackiness (which is probably why they are more comfortable than many mattes that dry down fully). Unfortunately, that means the wear time is not great. I put Sweet Cheeks on just before a meeting at 11, had a coffee (no visible transfer, which made me hope for a long wear time) and a yogurt for lunch, and as you can see in my pic, only the outer portion survived. I suppose if you are suuuuper careful, you might be able to have it survive a meal, but I wouldn't wear this on a date or an outing as I would feel the need to constantly reapply. All that said, I am keeping Kiss because I think she's a great color on me and I struggle to find pinks that don't clash with my pink cheeks. I do think the colors look quite different from how they appear on Ulta and Nudestix's websites, so if you can, try them in person. As much as I love supporting women-owned brands, I'm disappointed Nudestix has not changed their practices with regard to excess packaging. Yes, it's nice to have a little mirror and I try to find ways to repurpose the metal cases these come in, but it is really unnecessary and inevitably, they will end up in landfills. Couldn't they at least offer the option of no case? Maybe a thin cardboard one that's recyclable/biodegradable?

headline: Definately will buy again
comments:
I recently had the opportunity to try out the nudestix Intense Matte Lip + Cheek Pencil in the shade Sunkissed Pink, and I must say, I'm quite impressed with its performance. This versatile product is designed to be used on both the lips and cheeks, making it a convenient and multipurpose addition to any makeup routine.

headline: Long Lasting Lip Stain
comments:
I used the Beetroot Cheek and Lip tint primarily as a lip tint. WOW did it last!! Initially when applied to the lips it gives a very vibrant coral pink and red hue that is a little too overwhelming for my taste but when I wiped the lip tint off with a towel and pursed my lips together moving the lip tint around it was a beautiful shade that was perfect for summer.
A Tip- the tint is extremely long lasting (By long lasting I mean almost all day with eating and drinking), with that being said it is also somewhat staining. Precisely apply because I found out if I got it out of where it should be applied, it did not easily wipe off and the stain was still there along with my lipstick for a lot of the day. Also be careful on what the lip tint gets on (fingers, clothes, porous countertops, etc) as it is difficult to get off.
This review was collected as part of a promotion.

headline: Light weight
comments: The Ere Perez beetroot cheek and lip tinted came in the color Joy. Joy is a bright cherry red color that has a bit of an orange tint to the color. The applicator is strong and not flimsy. When applying it on my lips it went on smooth and covered a good portion of my lips with one swipe. As the product is a tint multiple layers were needed to cover the area and have a build up to be an even layer. The product is light weight and because of that it feels as if you aren't wearing anything on your lips. The color is bright and very pigmented and because of that I choose to not try it on my cheeks. I tried it out after eating and learned that it does not fade evenly. My lips did feel hydrated and unlike other tints didn't have a dry feeling. The finish is a bit glossy rather than a matte color.

headline: Just okay
comments:
As someone who has been in the beauty world for 10 years I've gotten the opportunity to try a variety of different products. I am one of the pickiest people when it comes to lip products because my lips are dry and very tiny. I usually don't wear much or any lip color because it tends to easily go over my lip lines looking very obvious. First off this formula was very thin, to be expected from a lip tint. For me it didn't offer any hydration (which I wasn't expecting) and it actually like balled up or started peeling on my lips. It was further disappointing because it kept getting on anything I touched my lips to or brushed them against even after letting it dry down. It also washed off pretty easily too. The color was nice but too dark for my personal preference. Overall I won't be reaching for this but if you like lip tint you might enjoy it.

headline: New shade - Jam
comments:
I love my Persona blushes, Bubble and Carmel, so I didn't hesitate to buy Jam when it launched but unfortunately, it's not nearly as good as the others. The powder itself feels more loosely pressed so that even the lightest tap of my brush produces significant kickup. This kickup combined with the excess powder needing to be knocked off my brush means a lot of product is lost.  
Jam is a beautiful midtoned cool berry color but sadly, it's difficult to blend and quickly becomes patchy on the skin, leaving harsh lines and/or a spot where the brush initially touched. I tried multiple natural and synthetic brushes, using the smallest amount possible and applying it over various base products as well as bare skin but it never blended seamlessly like Bubble and Carmel. 
I have lots of experience with trickier products as although I'm very fair, I have many blushes in deep and bright shades but the problems I had with this seem like formula issues specific to Jam. That said, I definitely recommend the other shades in this line.

headline: Love the mission
comments:
I appreciated this cheek and lip stain for how pigmented and long lasting it was on both my cheeks and lips. I put it on in the morning and was out in the sun all day and it was still very present on my skin and lips when I got home several hours later. 

The stain is very easy to use on lips, but more difficult to use on cheeks. Having largely used cream blushes, it took several uses to get adapted to the lack of blend-ability for this product. I also need to find another applicator to try to use, as I usually use my fingers to blend out products and as an applicator, but this product stained them. 

I do really appreciate the high quality of both the packaging and the product itself, as well as the mission of the brand Ere Perez and this product as a whole.

headline: Long Lasting Lip Stain
comments:
I used the Beetroot Cheek and Lip tint primarily as a lip tint. WOW did it last!! Initially when applied to the lips it gives a very vibrant coral pink and red hue that is a little too overwhelming for my taste but when I wiped the lip tint off with a towel and pursed my lips together moving the lip tint around it was a beautiful shade that was perfect for summer.
A Tip- the tint is extremely long lasting (By long lasting I mean almost all day with eating and drinking), with that being said it is also somewhat staining. Precisely apply because I found out if I got it out of where it should be applied, it did not easily wipe off and the stain was still there along with my lipstick for a lot of the day. Also be careful on what the lip tint gets on (fingers, clothes, porous countertops, etc) as it is difficult to get off.
This review was collected as part of a promotion.

headline: Light weight
comments: The Ere Perez beetroot cheek and lip tinted came in the color Joy. Joy is a bright cherry red color that has a bit of an orange tint to the color. The applicator is strong and not flimsy. When applying it on my lips it went on smooth and covered a good portion of my lips with one swipe. As the product is a tint multiple layers were needed to cover the area and have a build up to be an even layer. The product is light weight and because of that it feels as if you aren't wearing anything on your lips. The color is bright and very pigmented and because of that I choose to not try it on my cheeks. I tried it out after eating and learned that it does not fade evenly. My lips did feel hydrated and unlike other tints didn't have a dry feeling. The finish is a bit glossy rather than a matte color.

headline: Just okay

headline: Pleasantly surprised!
comments:
As someone new to the world of tints, I was so excited to try this. I was curious to see how it would compare to traditional blushes and lipsticks. 

Starting with thr basics, the packaging: it is sleek and minimalist, which I appreciate. The compact size makes it easy to carry in my purse, perfect for on-the-go touch-ups.
Applying the tint was straightforward, even for a beginner like me. The product glides smoothly onto both cheeks and lips. I found that using my fingers to blend the tint gave me the best results, providing a natural, flushed look. The color is buildable, so you can go for a subtle hint of color or a more dramatic pop, depending on your preference. It left mr with a vibrant, rosy hue that looks very natural on my skin. I got shade "joy" which i was worried would be too bright and clownish on me. But it turned out to be a versatile shade that I think would complement a variety of skin tones. The texture is lightweight and not sticky, which I loved. It feels comfortable on the skin and doesn't dry out my lips, a common issue I've had with other lip products.
I was also quite impressed with the staying power. It lasted several hours on both my cheeks and lips without the need for reapplication. Even after a meal, the color on my lips faded gracefully, leaving a nice stain rather than completely disappearing.

Overall, I am thrilled with this product! As my first foray into tints, it has set the bar high. The ease of use, natural finish, and impressive longevity make it a fantastic addition to my makeup routine. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a versatile, high-quality tint that enhances natural beauty.

I would definitely recommend to start small with application and add more as needed especially on the cheeks as this was just a lot of color at once. I applied dots on my face and lips then blended them out with my finger. My finger was very stained red but I was able to blend it out well on my cheeks and lips best with my finger. I don't really like wearing red on my lips or face but this gave me a nice flushed appearance and looked very natural. I love that this product uses a lot of natural ingredients and it is really buildable if you want more rich coloring on your lips or face! I think you have to remember that it is not a lipstick or lip gloss and adjust your expectations and usage with this in mind! It does what it's supposed to do! Was certainly a nice product and my first of its kind I've tried! Definitely worth a try!

headline: Lips > Cheeks
comments:
I am a retired crunchy beauty babe. I will always happily use natural based beauty products, however, I'm very tired these days, and got to a point where it wasn't great for my mental health to focus on all the good, bad, and ugly ingredients out there. That being said, Ere Perez really appeals to that natural loving part of my personality, and I was so excited to try the beetroot tint.
I definitely found some pros and cons with the product, and was left with mixed feelings. She's very pigmented, which is great! I on the other hand, am lacking in the pigment department. I really wanted to like this as a cheek tint or blush, but it appears this is either very much the wrong color for me, I lack the skills necessary to apply it properly, or a combination of both. I tried a few times with various tools, and I don't think we're meant to be a blush relationship.  I am curious about using the stain on my cheeks as part of a tantour situation, but I still think the red is probably just too red for me in this scenario. 
Just because we can't have a cheeky relationship doesn't mean we can't work things out! I really like the beetroot tint as a lip stain! I have been in a brown lip era, so it was a bit of a shock to my senses when I first popped it on as lip color, but it made me remember that sometimes a true red lip is what you need. (Plus, a red lip is a great way to say "eff you" to fascism if you're familiar with the history of a red lip.) The stain on its own is a really lovely true red. It is sticky for a moment, but that texture wipes off to a long lasting stain. After a few wears, I realized that it will calm down to a more casual dark pink on its own. I would avoid eating a greasy snack while wearing it unless you're ready to reapply after. 
It has a very mild non offensive flavor when applied - slightly sweet and not very beet-like. Also, it was partner approved. Inappropriate comments were made by him, so I believe he rates it 5 stars. I really hope Ere Perez expands the beetroot line into more colors, so maybe I can find the right cheek shade down the road.

headline: Versatile in color
comments:
I noticed all the photo reviews of this product are trash and not very helpful. Even the photos of the palette from the site and website aren't too helpful for what this is. I am using the app and realize there's no option to upload a photo as well, so let me explain what you get exactly to aid your decision in purchasing this palette. 

I am happy with the four tones. They are quite different from one another. The first blush on the very left is a pink. It is metallic bright baby pink with blue glitter overspray. Yes, the actual blush is metallic. Like a highlighter. It is not just the overspray. 

The second shade from the left is a warm rose shade. It is less metallic than the pink first one and definitely has a more natural appearance. It has a gold glitter overspray. 

The 3rd shade is a peachy tone with a champagne glitter overspray. It is metallic like the rest of them. 

The last shade is the one that surprised me the most. It is a deep red shade, a burgundy in the pan. It would suit deeper skin tones for sure.  Again, it is metallic and has a gold glitter overspray. 

There's actually not that much glitter overspray as I imagined from reading other reviews. HOWEVER, The shades are metallic (some more than others), so they will give a sheen off your cheeks. The first and last shade are the most highlighter-like shades. 

I am fair-light in skin tone and I am happy with this purchase. I didn't know what I was getting. It is a good value. It would work with even much deeper skin tones due to the sheen and reflection of color that it offers. 

It is not bad. Just know what you're getting. That is shiny blushes with a little bit of glitter. Great value. 

If you want a matte finish, this is NOT for you. And these blushes can actually look natural, except for the first and last shade (too reflective). The 2nd and 3rd blushes give a healthy glow.

comments: I just have a few thoughts about this blush (I am reviewing the shade "berry beautiful"):1. My only concern is the use of AHAs. Don't get me wrong, I love a good AHA in my routine, but I find the inclusion of retinol and lactic acid to be a superfluous addition to the formula. There is even a disclaimer on the back of the packaging about the ingredients causing photosensitivity, or something to that effect. I am very fair and burn even after a few minutes exposed in the sun without protection. After wearing this blush out in the wild and not touching up my SPF throughout the day, I feel that the skin on my cheeks feel mildly burnt and a little sensitive. Again, this could be me second-guessing myself, but I think I have valid reason for concern. I'm hesitant, but I like this blush a lot and will continue to try to make it work throughout the summer months. headline: Sunburnt Blush

headline: Spp
comments: I gave this Pur skin perfecting powder a whirl and as an esthetician for over 13 years I enjoyed the anti-aging aspect of the formulation however there's a few things about this product that didn't quite work for me. First of all blushing act in shade Berry beautiful is a pretty shade but is definitely too dark for my cool very fair skin to use as a blush. I tried blending it with my eyeshadow under my eyes but the finished result looked a little muddy and lack-luster if I'm being honest. I also tried it as a flush of color all over the lids which did look a lot better but I found it to be hard to blend and kind of patchy and had to blend another shade on to the lid to make it look more even and cohesive. I felt the color payoff could've been better as well as the evenness of the pigment. The shade is pretty but as a "multi-tasking" product it left a lot to be desired. I think if this is a shade that compliments you, you could probably make it work as a blush but there are better options on the market that I personally would go for over this. I do love that it's formulated without fillers, fragrance or dyes but for the price tag I expected more and for that reason I don't recommend this product. Also one last thing I will say is I don't like the material they used for the lid as it does cause you to leave finger prints and smudge marks any time you touch it which is a minor flaw but something I felt was worth noting as it is not my preference.   **This review was created through an educational promotional event hosted between the brand and beauty experts.**

The WYN lip and cheek color is a very nice formula that really blends into the skin and gives a very natural  looking flush. A little goes a long way. I removed one star because the color description seemed off- I was expecting more pink but SOAR is more of reddish brown in my opinion. I prefer that color for my lips over my cheeks but again overall I am very happy with the product and the packaging is fun and easy to apply.

headline: Easily my favorite product from this line!

headline: Gloppy and wears unevenly
comments: Such a bust.  I was so excited to try these and ordered 3.  The colors are bold which is great but there is too much product on the wand when it leaves the tube.  It is really hard to apply so much product with any precision. Initially it creates a very glossy finish but it takes a long time to dry down - I would give you the exact time but I could only give it 5 minutes before I had to blot it.  Even after blotted it transfers easily for another few minutes until it is set.  After all that it makes a nice stain but that wears off quickly so for me this was not worth it.

I know it is pricey, but the bronzer is huge, so I don't mind the price point, especially since you don't need to use a lot since the color payoff is so great. It is really hard for me to find a bronzer that actually works for me since I am so pale and I have dry skin. So I absolutely recommend the fair shade if you are pale like me!

It actually wasn't too dark, I went in very light handed with my brush and it blends out like a dream but gave me the most gorgeous sun kissed glow. Normally, I play it super safe and go with the lightest shade in every single bronzer but I think if you are fair, you absolutely can get away with the shade 2 or 3. That is a testament to how good this product is, it's not orange at all. The texture is unbelievable-so creamy that you just need a slight dab of your brush and you can build as needed. This will last me forever, so price wise, if I HAD to purchase it myself, it would be worth every penny. Plus, the packaging and mirror are lovely.

headline: Underrated bronzer
comments:
I'm super impressed with this bronzer! I bought it on a whim without doing much research and ended up loving it! 

Powder bronzers don't get enough love anymore and brands seem to only come out with cream and liquid formulas now. I personally still love powder bronzers but I feel like it's hard to find a formula that isn't too powdery, is buildable, blends easily, and doesn't get muddy or patchy. 

This formula is more of a creamy powder if that makes sense, when I swirl my brush in the pan it doesn't get overly powdery or apply unevenly, which has been a major issue for a lot of powder bronzers I've tried. 

The shade is a beautiful natural bronze, not orange whatsoever but definitely not cool toned. I have light-medium skin, I purchased the 05 shade but was worried it might be a little too dark (they were out of the 04 shade), but it's absolutely perfect. 

Overall, this is by far the best bronzer I've tried and I definitely will repurchase.

headline: Underrated bronzer
comments:
I'm super impressed with this bronzer! I bought it on a whim without doing much research and ended up loving it! 

Powder bronzers don't get enough love anymore and brands seem to only come out with cream and liquid formulas now. I personally still love powder bronzers but I feel like it's hard to find a formula that isn't too powdery, is buildable, blends easily, and doesn't get muddy or patchy. 

This formula is more of a creamy powder if that makes sense, when I swirl my brush in the pan it doesn't get overly powdery or apply unevenly, which has been a major issue for a lot of powder bronzers I've tried. 

The shade is a beautiful natural bronze, not orange whatsoever but definitely not cool toned. I have light-medium skin, I purchased the 05 shade but was worried it might be a little too dark (they were out of the 04 shade), but it's absolutely perfect. 

Overall, this is by far the best bronzer I've tried and I definitely will repurchase.

headline: Fair shade is amazing
comments: I have fair skin, I'm talking the 00 concealer shade of Dior. This bronzer is fantastic for cool tones and isn't orange at all. It blends wonderfully and is a creamy formula. I know it is pricey, but the bronzer is huge, so I don't mind the price point, especially since you don't need to use a lot since the color payoff is so great. It is really hard for me to find a bronzer that actually works for me since I am so pale and I have dry skin. So I absolutely recommend the fair shade if you are pale like me!
